tldr: The paper introduces double-randomized quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) using randomized block-encodings and random polynomials to reduce circuit depth for early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
motivation: Block-encoding subroutine depth is a major bottleneck for applying QSVT to quantum chemistry and condensed-matter problems on early fault-tolerant hardware.
method: The authors split a linear operator into a core operator and a tail, then block-encode a normalized sum of the core and an average of randomly sampled tail terms; they combine this with random QSVT polynomials and derive diamond-norm error bounds.
result: They show that randomized block-encoding and polynomial randomization yield multiplicative circuit-depth savings with only additive error contributions, and numerically demonstrate order-of-magnitude reductions in Pauli terms for long-range Heisenberg and iron-sulfur complex Hamiltonians.
conclusion: The approach paves the way for QSVT demonstrations on early fault-tolerant quantum hardware by making block-encoding more resource-efficient.

title: The Ordered Sum-rank Metric And Linearized Multiplicity Codes: Nrt Meets Sum-rank
authors: Umberto Mart\'inez-Pe\~nas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce linearized multiplicity codes, which are a common generalization of linearized Reed--Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. We also introduce the ordered sum-rank metric, which is a common generalization of the sum-rank metric and the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric (or ordered Hamming metric). We provide a Singleton bound for the ordered sum-rank metric and show that linearized multiplicity codes attain it. That is, they are maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes. We introduce the support lattice for the ordered sum-rank metric and study duality, support distributions and weight distributions of MOSRD codes. We also show that MOSRD codes are ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under some divisibility conditions, MSRD (and thus MDS). For linear MOSRD codes, we give lower bounds on the field extension degree by the number of matrix columns, and upper bounds on the block length by the base field size. We conclude by showing that linearized multiplicity codes attain such bounds exactly in almost all cases, and the same growth order in all cases.
tldr: The paper introduces linearized multiplicity codes and the ordered sum-rank metric, a common generalization of the sum-rank and Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metrics, and constructs codes attaining a Singleton-type bound.
motivation: Sum-rank and NRT metrics each capture distinct notions of non-uniform error and erasure patterns; a unified framework would consolidate these coding-theoretic tools and extend linearized Reed–Solomon and univariate multiplicity codes.
method: The authors define the ordered sum-rank metric, prove a Singleton bound for it, and introduce linearized multiplicity codes as a common generalization of linearized Reed–Solomon and multiplicity codes; they further develop a support lattice to analyze duality, support and weight distributions.
result: Linearized multiplicity codes are shown to be maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes, hence ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under divisibility conditions, MSRD/MDS; bounds on field extension degree versus matrix columns and on block length versus base field size are derived and attained by these codes in almost all cases.
conclusion: The work unifies several classical coding metrics and code families and provides optimal constructions with essentially tight parameter bounds, but remains purely classical coding theory with no quantum information-theoretic component.

title: Scalable And Interpretable Quantum Mixture Of Experts For High-Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data
authors: Junghoon Justin Park, Anna Jung, Kyumin Lee, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Shinjae Yoo, Jiook Cha
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Mixture of Experts (QMoE) architectures offer a promising path toward scalable quantum machine learning, yet existing approaches remain largely confined to low-dimensional benchmarks and often rely on naive input partitioning that disrupts feature dependencies. We address these gaps by introducing Feature-Partitioned QMoE, which partitions high-dimensional spatio-temporal inputs into functionally coherent feature groups and assigns each group to a dedicated quantum expert. We further propose a hierarchical interpretability framework that leverages the modular structure of QMoE to produce circuit-level gating analysis, per-expert gradient saliency, and heterogeneity-based subtype discovery. Applied to ADHD classification from resting-state fMRI (N=4,458, ABCD Study, 180 brain ROIs, 363 timepoints), the proposed Theory-Driven QMoE achieves performance comparable to matched-capacity classical and quantum baselines while enabling circuit-attributable interpretation. The framework identifies FDR-corrected ADHD-associated biomarkers in executive-control and anterior default-mode networks and reveals three neurobiologically meaningful ADHD subtypes. These results position Feature-Partitioned QMoE as a scalable and interpretable methodology for applying quantum machine learning to high-dimensional biomedical data.
tldr: The paper introduces a Feature-Partitioned Quantum Mixture of Experts architecture with hierarchical interpretability for high-dimensional spatio-temporal fMRI data, applied to ADHD classification.
motivation: Existing quantum mixture-of-experts models are limited to low-dimensional benchmarks and use naive input partitioning that disrupts feature dependencies, while scalability and interpretability for high-dimensional biomedical data remain underexplored.
method: The authors partition spatio-temporal inputs into functionally coherent feature groups, assign each to a dedicated quantum expert, and develop a hierarchical interpretability framework covering circuit-level gating, per-expert gradient saliency, and heterogeneity-based subtype discovery.
result: On resting-state fMRI data from 4,458 ABCD participants, the Theory-Driven QMoE matches classical and quantum baselines while identifying FDR-corrected ADHD biomarkers in executive-control and anterior default-mode networks and revealing three ADHD subtypes.
conclusion: Feature-Partitioned QMoE is presented as a scalable and interpretable methodology for quantum machine learning on high-dimensional biomedical data, though its contribution is primarily applied and domain-specific rather than advancing quantum information theory.

title: Advancing Quantum Reinforcement Learning With Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search And Adaptive Non-local Observables
authors: Junghoon Justin Park, Kyumin Lee, Anna Jung, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Shinjae Yoo, Jiook Cha
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ans\"atze. Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) address these issues independently, but to our knowledge have not been combined or compared in a single QRL framework. We present an ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the Quantum Time-series Transformer (QTSTransformer), evaluated on a 2 x 2 factorial design across six environments--two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games. Three findings emerge. First, the quantum agent outperforms a matched classical transformer baseline on five of six environments, with absolute scores ranging from 360.0 vs 304.0 (MarioBros) to 17.2 vs 2.5 (Breakout), while using approximately 12.5x fewer transformer parameters on the four Atari environments (more modestly so on the two classic-control tasks). Second, ANO and DiffQAS provide complementary benefits: ANO yields the largest gain on continuous-state CartPole (347.7 vs 223.2), while DiffQAS yields the largest absolute Atari gains (Breakout 17.2 vs 3.0; DonkeyKong 70.0 vs 37.0). Third, combining both innovations exhibits an asymmetric interaction: ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS, whereas DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade when ANO is added. These results provide design guidance for QRL agents: select between ANO and DiffQAS according to whether the bottleneck is the measurement basis or the gate topology, rather than applying both indiscriminately.
tldr: An ablation study combining Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) inside a Quantum Time-series Transformer for quantum reinforcement learning across six control and Atari environments.
motivation: Variational quantum circuit-based QRL is limited by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed ansätze; ANO and DiffQAS address these separately but have not been combined or compared in a single framework.
method: A 2x2 factorial ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the QTSTransformer architecture, benchmarked against a matched classical transformer baseline on two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games.
result: The quantum agent beats the classical baseline on five of six environments with ~12.5x fewer transformer parameters on Atari; ANO helps most on CartPole, DiffQAS on Atari, and their combination shows an asymmetric interaction where ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS but DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade with ANO.
conclusion: Practitioners should choose ANO or DiffQAS depending on whether the bottleneck is measurement basis or gate topology rather than applying both, offering design guidance for QRL agents.

title: Exact Redundancy Under Average And Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints
authors: Yijun Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, we establish the asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under the average distortion constraint, the coefficient is half of the minimum probability that an output reveals information about the source, among all rate-distortion optimal channels. Under the almost-sure distortion constraint, the coefficient is either [MATH] or [MATH], depending on whether the [MATH]-tilted information is constant or not. Both converse results follow from a common change-of-measure inequality. Finally, we verify the required conditions under both distortion requirements always hold for finite alphabets.
tldr: The paper characterizes exact redundancy for lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints.
motivation: It aims to refine rate-distortion theory by determining the precise asymptotic redundancy beyond the rate-distortion limit under two distortion criteria.
method: The analysis derives converse bounds via a common change-of-measure inequality and evaluates optimal channel-dependent quantities under regularity conditions.
result: Under average distortion the redundancy coefficient is half the minimum probability that an output reveals source information among optimal channels; under almost-sure distortion it depends on whether tilted information is constant.
conclusion: The required regularity conditions are shown to always hold for finite alphabets, yielding exact redundancy characterizations in that setting.

title: Entropy-Based And Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics For Informed Dynamic Scheduling Of Belief-Propagation Decoding For Ldpc Codes
authors: Tofar Chih-Yuan Chang, Chia-En Liu, Ying-Ren Jian, Di-Chun Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose two enhanced conditional innovation (CI) metrics for informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) in belief-propagation (BP) decoding of LDPC codes. The CI-based residual BP (CIRBP) algorithm uses the CI metric to guide the selection of the variable node (VN) to be updated and has been shown to outperform several existing IDS-based BP decoders, especially at the early decoding stage. However, the original CI metric uses only the absolute difference between the current and precomputed posterior probabilities and does not separately account for the reliability associated with each probability. By reformulating the CI metric relative to the decision boundary, we separate each posterior probability into its decision side and a linear-distance term reflecting reliability. Replacing the latter with the binary entropy complement yields the proposed entropy-based CI (E-CI) metric. Moreover, the proposed quadratic CI (Q-CI) metric is derived from the leading quadratic term in the local expansion of the entropy complement, avoiding the logarithmic operations required for direct E-CI evaluation. We apply both proposed metrics to the CIRBP decoder and its node-wise variant. Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally provide lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with their relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.
tldr: The paper proposes entropy-based and quadratic conditional innovation metrics to guide informed dynamic scheduling in belief-propagation decoding of classical LDPC codes.
motivation: The original conditional innovation metric for residual belief propagation uses only posterior-probability differences and does not separately account for the reliability of each probability, limiting scheduling decisions.
method: The authors reformulate the conditional innovation metric relative to the decision boundary, replace the linear-distance reliability term with the binary entropy complement, and derive a quadratic approximation that avoids logarithmic operations.
result: Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally yield lower frame error rates than the original conditional innovation metric, with relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.
conclusion: Entropy-based and quadratic conditional innovation metrics can improve dynamic scheduling for classical LDPC belief-propagation decoding, but the work has no direct quantum information component.

title: A Proof Of The Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz Conjecture On Entropy Maximization For Cube Projections
authors: Vu Khac Ky
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least [MATH]. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.
tldr: The paper completes the Eskenazis–Nayar–Tkocz conjecture by proving that differential entropy among one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube is maximized exactly in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes, covering the remaining low dimensions via computer-assisted certified proofs.
motivation: Pang had established the conjecture for all dimensions above a threshold, leaving small dimensions open; the authors close this gap and strengthen the result with quantitative stability estimates.
method: Polynomial entropy bounds are derived for dimensions three through six, combined with exact rational-arithmetic certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density and certified one-dimensional numerical integration.
result: The conjecture is proved in the remaining dimensions, quantitative stability estimates are obtained, and the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound is determined.
conclusion: The work settles a purely classical/geometric entropy-maximization problem with rigorous computer-assisted verification, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: New Constructions Of Optimal Ferrers Diagram Rank-metric Codes For Quasi-block Monotone Ferrers Diagrams
authors: Yong Jin, Yuhao Ning, Dengming Xu, Chengming Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constant dimension subspace codes (CDCs) have become an important object in coding theory due to their applications in random network coding. The paper is devoted to constructing optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block Ferrers diagrams, which play a crucial role in the multilevel construction of CDCs. Let \(_q\) be the finite field with \(q\) elements of characteristic \(p\), \(P\) be a power of \(p\), and \(e\) be a positive integer. Let \(L=\mathbb F_{q^{eP}}\) and \(\sigma\) be the Frobenius \(\mathbb F_q\)-automorphism of \(L\), set \(N=\sigma^e-\). Based on the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of the nilpotent map \(N\), we construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block monotone diagrams. Specifically, considering \(n \times l\) Ferrers diagrams, we prove that optimal codes always exist for block monotone diagrams when \(n = eP\). Furthermore, by employing puncturing on columns, we prove that optimal codes also always exist for block strictly monotone diagrams, removing the restriction \(n = eP\). Consequently, optimal codes always exist for block upper triangular diagrams, specifically for maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD)-constructible block diagram pairs, which generalizes the corresponding results in , in which the rank distance or the characteristic is restricted. Furthermore, by employing both puncturing and shortening on columns, we prove that optimal codes always exist for quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams, thereby generalizing the corresponding results in . The optimal codes constructed in this paper will potentially be beneficial to the further construction of CDCs.
tldr: The paper constructs optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams, with applications to constant dimension subspace codes in random network coding.
motivation: Constant dimension subspace codes are important for random network coding, and optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are needed for multilevel constructions of such codes.
method: The authors use the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of a nilpotent map and employ puncturing and shortening on columns to construct optimal codes for block monotone, block strictly monotone, and quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams.
result: They prove existence of optimal codes for block monotone diagrams when n=eP, remove this restriction for block strictly monotone diagrams via puncturing, and extend existence to quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams using puncturing and shortening.
conclusion: The constructed codes generalize prior results on MSRD-constructible block diagram pairs and may be useful for further constructions of constant dimension subspace codes.

title: Error-correcting Codes Without Parity-check Bits
authors: Boris Ryabko, Ivan Baksheev, Vyacheslav Zhuravlev
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We are developing a new approach to the problem of error correction in communication channels, in which the input sequence is transformed in such a way that the interdependence of symbols increases significantly. Then, after the sequence is transmitted over the channel, this property is used for error correction, so that the residual error rate is significantly reduced. A natural example of its application is the transmission of binary sequences whose entropy (per symbol) is less than one, since in this case the length of the transmitted sequence remains constant during encoding and decoding. An algorithm has been developed to implement the maximum likelihood method, in which the encoding and decoding times are linear. This algorithm was used to experimentally investigate its effectiveness on popular channel models, and it was found that there are certain sets of parameters for which the proposed method is quite effective.
tldr: The authors propose a classical error-correction scheme that omits parity-check bits and instead relies on deliberately increased statistical interdependence among transmitted symbols, decoding via a linear-time maximum-likelihood algorithm.
motivation: Standard error-correcting codes spend redundancy on explicit parity checks; the authors argue that redundancy can instead be hidden in the correlation structure of the source, which is natural for low-entropy binary sequences where encoding preserves length.
method: The input sequence is transformed so that symbol interdependence rises substantially; after transmission, this structure is exploited by a maximum-likelihood decoder implemented with linear encoding and decoding time, and the scheme is benchmarked experimentally on standard channel models.
result: Experiments on popular channel models show that for certain parameter regimes the method noticeably reduces residual error rates while keeping constant sequence length and linear complexity.
conclusion: Correlation-based redundancy is a viable alternative to parity-check coding in specific low-entropy settings, though the approach is classical and its advantages appear parameter-dependent.

title: Machine-learned Active Spaces Enable Quantum Calculations Of Spin-state Energetics Of Transition-metal Complexes On Quantum Hardware
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Sabre Kais, Werner Dobrautz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. The orbitals that belong in it are those that are strongly entangled in the correlated wavefunction, but measuring this entanglement requires the very correlated calculation that the active space is meant to make affordable. Here we present SpinAware, a machine-learning model that predicts density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution of each spin state, without any correlated calculation. Each of the 20 highest occupied and 20 lowest unoccupied orbitals is described by 60 descriptors computed from the UHF solution, among them the differences between its alpha and beta occupations and energies, its metal-d and ligand character, and its exchange coupling to the other orbitals, and a transformer predicts the entropy of each orbital in the context of all others. Trained on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations on mononuclear Cr-Ni complexes, the model transfers to experimentally characterized complexes with ligands, binding topologies, oxidation states and metals absent from training. Over 11 spin states it reproduces the DMRG entropy profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.027, and combining the predicted entropies with the predicted mutual information gives a candidate pool that contains 99% of the DMRG-active orbitals of the benchmark spin states while keeping, on average, only 15 of the 40 orbitals. Natural-orbital occupation scans then select compact active spaces from this pool for a nickel and a cobalt complex. Sample-based quantum diagonalization with samples from IBM quantum processors reproduces the exact CASCI energies of these spaces to within 0.3 kcal/mol and their spin-state gaps to within 0.10 kcal/mol for up to 32 qubits.
tldr: SpinAware uses machine learning to predict DMRG orbital entropies from UHF solutions, enabling compact active-space selection for quantum calculations of transition-metal spin-state energetics.
motivation: Multireference quantum chemistry on classical or quantum hardware requires active-space selection, but measuring the relevant orbital entanglement normally requires the expensive correlated calculation the active space is meant to simplify.
method: The authors train a transformer on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations to predict single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from UHF-derived descriptors, then use natural-orbital occupation scans to select active spaces for sample-based quantum diagonalization on IBM processors.
result: The model predicts DMRG entropy profiles with mean absolute error 0.027, retains 99% of DMRG-active orbitals while keeping on average only 15 of 40 orbitals, and quantum diagonalization reproduces CASCI energies within 0.3 kcal/mol and spin-state gaps within 0.10 kcal/mol for up to 32 qubits.
conclusion: Machine-learned active spaces make quantum chemistry calculations of transition-metal spin-state energetics more feasible on quantum hardware, but the work is primarily a quantum-chemistry application rather than a contribution to the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems directions.

title: On The Power-Law Duality In Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
authors: Hassan Hassanabadi Georg Junker
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we first revisit the Hooke-Newton duality and its generalisation to arbitrary power laws in classical and quantum mechanics. We then consider Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics on the real line, which is a deformation of standard Heisenberg-Schr\"odinger quantum mechanics closely related to Dunkl's differential-difference operator formalism. We consider the corresponding eigenvalue problem for the harmonic potential and a Coulomb-like potential. We observe that the Hooke-Newton duality is also applicable to these deformed quantum systems allowing us to solve the eigenvalue problem of one by mapping it onto the other system. This approach is then generalised to arbitrary power-law potentials in Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics. Whereas in standard quantum mechanics the classical re-scaling of angular momenta has to be applied to Langer-modified quantum angular momenta, Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics requires a rescaling of deformation parameters similar to the Langer-type modification but involving the reflection operator. The energy coupling-constant exchange, however, remains the same in all three cases, classical mechanics, quantum mechanics and Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics.
tldr: The paper extends the classical Hooke-Newton (power-law) duality to Wigner-Yang deformed quantum mechanics, whose algebra involves Dunkl-type reflection operators, and uses it to map solvable harmonic and Coulomb-like eigenvalue problems onto one another.
motivation: The Hooke-Newton duality relating power-law potentials is well understood classically and in standard quantum mechanics, but its fate under deformed quantum formalisms such as Wigner-Yang mechanics, which involve reflection operators and modified angular momenta, was unclear.
method: The authors revisit the classical rescaling of angular momenta and its quantum Langer-type modification, then formulate the analogous rescaling in Wigner-Yang quantum mechanics using Dunkl differential-difference operators, solving the harmonic and Coulomb-like eigenvalue problems by duality mapping for arbitrary power laws.
result: The duality is shown to persist in Wigner-Yang mechanics, but requires a rescaling of the deformation parameters involving the reflection operator, in place of the Langer modification of angular momenta; the energy coupling-constant exchange relation remains identical across classical, quantum, and Wigner-Yang cases.
conclusion: Power-law dualities are a structural feature robust to Wigner-Yang deformation, providing a route to exact spectra for deformed potentials, though the deformation parameters rather than angular momenta absorb the required rescalings.

title: Finding Low-Energy States Of The Bernasconi Model Via Simulated Transverse-Field Quantum Dynamics
authors: Rudranil Basu Shaashwat Sagar Kale
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequence (LABS) problem, the ground-state problem of the Bernasconi model, has a rugged landscape with deep, isolated local minima. We study real-time transverse-field dynamics initialized in these minima as a means of reaching lower-energy configurations. Using GPU statevector simulation for N = 20-30 spins, we compare the escape probability per verified quantum sample with the success rate per energy evaluation of steepest-descent kicks, random restarts and tabu search. Using the same field and sampling window across all system sizes, we find that, relative to the best classical baseline, the sampler achieves a factor of 11.9-35.2 for the deepest traps and 13.4-27.2 for the next energy tier. These ratios describe a constant-factor improvement in sample efficiency over the sizes studied. At the adopted field, broad Hamming-space spreading coexists with a strong preference for low-energy states. This regime follows a sharp increase in displacement as the field is raised. To connect this behaviour to the landscape, a short-time expansion relates the onset of escape to target distance and intermediate energies. Bounds on isotropic spin flips and on the free transverse mixer quantify the role of the Bernasconi potential in the observed transfer. At N = 28, the ground-state probability at t = 30 exceeds a canonical cost prediction fitted to the same mean energy by a factor of about 1.9. The cost of generating each quantum sample is assessed separately through a hardware estimate, which places a direct circuit implementation two to three orders of magnitude beyond present processor capabilities.
tldr: The paper uses GPU statevector simulation of transverse-field quantum dynamics to escape deep local minima in the Bernasconi/LABS optimization landscape and compares sample efficiency with classical heuristics.
motivation: The Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequence problem has a rugged energy landscape with isolated deep traps, motivating quantum-inspired dynamics as a way to reach lower-energy configurations.
method: Real-time transverse-field dynamics is initialized in local minima and simulated for N=20-30 spins using GPU statevector methods, with escape probabilities compared against steepest-descent kicks, random restarts, and tabu search.
result: The sampler shows constant-factor improvements in sample efficiency over the best classical baseline for the deepest traps, but direct circuit implementation is estimated to be two to three orders of magnitude beyond current hardware capabilities.
conclusion: Transverse-field dynamics can improve sampling efficiency for LABS at the studied sizes, though the approach remains far from practical quantum hardware implementation.

title: When The Boundary Changes The Bulk: Topological Edge Modes In Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: J. Sirker N. Sedlmayr
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in open chains it has been noted that the boundary can change the bulk: in time windows bounded by DQPTs, exponentially localized edge modes of the Loschmidt matrix produce a finite change in the intensive return rate. These modes have been attributed to topological properties of the initial and final Hamiltonians. Here we show that it is not the topology of the Hamiltonians but rather that of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix which protects these edge modes. In particular, we show that topological edge modes can exist in class A, where both Hamiltonians are topologically trivial. For classes A, BDI, and AIII we show that these modes are protected by [MATH] indices of a Toeplitz operator and that K-splitting theorems provide a precise bulk-boundary correspondence. In class D, they are protected instead by a [MATH] index that records whether the quench has flipped the fermion parity at the edge. The bulk invariant for class D can be formulated either as a ratio of the Loschmidt amplitudes for periodic and anti-periodic boundary conditions or as a winding number that counts phase vortices in momentum and time. We discuss examples and provide numerical data for all four topological classes.
tldr: The paper shows that edge modes contributing to dynamical quantum phase transitions are protected by topological properties of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix rather than by the topology of the initial and final Hamiltonians.
motivation: Previous work observed that boundary effects can alter the bulk return rate in dynamical quantum phase transitions and attributed these effects to topological properties of the quench Hamiltonians. The authors aim to identify the correct topological origin of these edge modes.
method: The authors analyze the Loschmidt matrix for open chains and classify its edge modes using Toeplitz operator indices and K-splitting theorems for symmetry classes A, BDI, AIII, and D, supported by numerical examples.
result: They find that topological edge modes can exist even when both Hamiltonians are topologically trivial, as in class A, and derive bulk-boundary correspondences for classes A, BDI, and AIII. In class D, the modes are protected by a Z2 index recording fermion-parity flips at the edge.
conclusion: The protection of Loschmidt-matrix edge modes is governed by the non-Hermitian topology of the Loschmidt matrix itself, not by the topology of the quench Hamiltonians, refining the understanding of boundary effects in dynamical quantum phase transitions.

title: Exposing And Overcoming The Polarizability Pathology Of The Fermi-Omont Pseudopotential
authors: S. Efe G\"urleyen, Matthew T. Eiles, Chris H. Greene
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any realistic electron-atom or ion-atom potential energy function contains a long-range contribution from the atomic polarizability which gives a [MATH] long-range tail. This modifies the well-known Wigner threshold law for orbital momenta [MATH], causing these [MATH] scattering phase shifts to vary linearly in energy instead of as [MATH]. The [MATH] Fermi-Omont zero-range pseudopotentials are erroneously divergent at zero energy due to this modification, a divergence deriving from very long-range physics that should not be incorporated into a Dirac delta function. Here, we investigate some alternative scenario for repairing this pathological behavior to obtain smooth and accurate potential energy curves calculated using the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential concept, with some systematic benchmarking tests for comparison.
tldr: The paper diagnoses and proposes repairs for the zero-energy divergence of Fermi-Omont zero-range pseudopotentials caused by the long-range atomic polarizability tail in electron-atom and ion-atom scattering.
motivation: Realistic electron-atom and ion-atom potentials have a -α/(2r^4) long-range tail that modifies Wigner threshold laws for l ≥ 1, making standard Fermi-Omont pseudopotentials divergent at zero energy and thus unreliable for computing potential energy curves.
method: The authors analyze the origin of the pathological divergence and investigate alternative regularization schemes for the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential concept, benchmarking the resulting smooth potential energy curves systematically against reference calculations.
result: Several repair scenarios are compared and benchmarked, identifying formulations that remove the spurious zero-energy divergence while retaining accuracy of the pseudopotential description.
conclusion: Modified pseudopotential constructions can overcome the polarizability pathology, yielding smooth and accurate potential energy curves for ultracold scattering calculations.

title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
authors: Liyi Li, Mahir Anand, James Bryan Graves, Amr Sabry
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To find a [MATH]-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all [MATH] subsets of the [MATH] vertices, although only the subsets of size [MATH] can be answers. We present ENQ+, an AQC language in which the programmer writes both cost functions. Data constraints define the problem cost function. Relational constraints, a new construct, declare the moves the search may make between configurations and define the initial cost function. For the clique, a single relational constraint, which exchanges a chosen vertex with an unchosen one, confines the search to the subsets of size [MATH]. ENQ+ thereby turns constrained quantum annealing, which physicists set up by hand for individual problems, into a programming construct. We give ENQ+ a semantics in many-world configuration (MWC) graphs, whose nodes are configurations and whose edges are moves, and derive from it a step-wise semantics of adiabatic evolution. We prove that a run stays within the component of the MWC graph that contains its initial state, and that a run from an approximate initial state still reaches the answer, with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact one. We compile ENQ+ to quantum circuits, prove the compilation correct with respect to the semantics, and use ENQ+ to program the Three-Dimensional Matching, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Traveling Salesperson problems.
tldr: The paper introduces ENQ+, an adiabatic quantum programming language where programmers specify both initial and problem cost functions using data and relational constraints.
motivation: Existing adiabatic quantum computation languages fix the initial cost function, causing the search to range over all subsets rather than only valid configurations, which is inefficient for constrained problems such as clique.
method: The authors define relational constraints that encode allowed moves between configurations, give ENQ+ a many-world configuration graph semantics and a stepwise adiabatic-evolution semantics, and compile programs to quantum circuits with a correctness proof.
result: They prove that a run stays within the connected component of its initial state and that an approximate initial state reaches the answer with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact initial state; they also program Three-Dimensional Matching, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Traveling Salesperson.
conclusion: ENQ+ turns constrained quantum annealing into a programming construct with formal semantics and compilation, enabling structured adiabatic quantum programming for constrained combinatorial problems.

title: Log-optimal Two-sample Testing By Betting
authors: Aaditya Ramdas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is [MATH], where [MATH] is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit [MATH] when [MATH]. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.
tldr: The paper constructs a universal anytime-valid two-sample test based on betting (test martingales) whose asymptotic log-wealth growth rate is optimal for every pair of distributions and every limiting ratio of sample sizes.
motivation: Two-sample testing traditionally relies on batch p-values and fixed-sample-size analysis; the author wants an anytime-valid procedure that remains statistically efficient (log-optimal) uniformly across arbitrary distributions and sample-size regimes.
method: The author builds test martingales via logarithmic-loss betting and measurable characteristic kernels, refining finite partitions; the optimal log-wealth rate is identified with (weighted) Jensen-Shannon divergence, and universal constructions are given over standard Borel spaces.
result: For balanced independent pairs, the optimal growth rate equals the Jensen-Shannon divergence; unequal sample sizes yield weighted Jensen-Shannon information with the one-sample limit recovered, and continuous classifier fine-tuning is demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.
conclusion: The contribution is the generality of a single log-optimal anytime-valid two-sample procedure and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions, with practical classifier-based implementations.

title: Probing Equilibrium Properties With Gaussian States Beyond Mean-field
authors: Esther Cruz, J. Ignacio Cirac, Dominik S. Wild
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing equilibrium properties of interacting fermionic systems is central to many problems in condensed matter physics, yet computationally challenging. Mean-field methods tackle this problem by restricting to a tractable class of states, which, however, often fail to capture genuine many-body correlations. We illustrate this in the context of Gaussian mean-field methods by minimizing the energy variance of Gaussian states, showing that even states with the narrowest energy distributions poorly reproduce the microcanonical ensemble. To overcome this limitation, we develop a computationally efficient method to construct linear superpositions of Gaussian states whose energy variance can be systematically decreased by adding more terms to the superposition. We provide complementary results for the canonical ensemble, for which we propose a sampling algorithm based on convex combinations of Gaussian states. We benchmark our methods using the [MATH]--[MATH] model and find that both methods greatly outperform mean-field calculations. In particular, we obtain the correct critical exponents as well as a significantly improved estimate for the critical temperature. As an independent result, we prove a quantum Berry--Esseen theorem for fermionic Gaussian states, which states that the local density of states converges to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit without any assumptions about the spatial correlations of the state.
tldr: The paper develops Gaussian-state methods beyond mean-field to compute equilibrium properties of interacting fermionic systems and proves a quantum Berry-Esseen theorem for fermionic Gaussian states.
motivation: Mean-field Gaussian methods often fail to capture genuine many-body correlations and poorly reproduce microcanonical ensembles, motivating more accurate but tractable state representations.
method: The authors minimize energy variance over Gaussian states, construct linear superpositions of Gaussian states with systematically decreasing energy variance, and propose a convex-combination sampling algorithm for canonical ensembles.
result: Benchmarking on a fermionic model shows both methods outperform mean-field calculations, yielding correct critical exponents and a significantly improved critical-temperature estimate; they also prove a quantum Berry-Esseen theorem for fermionic Gaussian states.
conclusion: Superpositions and convex combinations of Gaussian states provide efficient improved tools for equilibrium fermionic many-body calculations beyond mean-field, with independent implications for the local density of states.

title: Gaussian Mass Inequalities For Lattices
authors: Minjia Shi, Xinguang Dai, Patrick Sol\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be [MATH] (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~[MATH] lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~[MATH] lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.
tldr: This paper proves Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices constructed from self-dual codes, with applications to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel.
motivation: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is relevant to lattice coding, and a conjectured bound for stable lattices motivates extending Kominers' Construction A result to other code constructions and extremal unimodular lattices.
method: The authors build on Kominers' bound to establish average inequalities for Construction D lattices from free self-dual quaternary codes and self-dual senary codes, and prove strict Gaussian-mass inequalities for extremal Type II and Type I unimodular lattices using theta truncation, shadow inversions, and translated-lattice inequalities.
result: They obtain averaging bounds over the genus of Type II lattices and extend the binary Construction A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under residue-code conditions.
conclusion: The work advances classical lattice coding theory and theta-series inequalities, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Treatment Of D-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians With Noninteger Quantum Numbers And Their Connection To The Radial Momentum Operator
authors: Z\"uhra G\"une\c{s} Ali Ba\u{g}c{\i}
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals, the generalization of Coulomb-Sturmians to noninteger quantum numbers, were recently identified as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians. In the present study, this identification is treated in detail. The radial differential equation for these orbitals is derived directly from their closed form. It represents the general Coulomb-Sturmian differential equation for quantum numbers with real values. The solution is verified through a power series representation and a first-order matrix form based on the Green's function of the radial Laplacian. New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.
tldr: The paper provides a detailed mathematical treatment of d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers and derives their connection to the radial momentum operator, uncertainty products, Shannon entropy, and Fisher information.
motivation: The authors aim to elaborate on the recent identification of Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians and to establish their differential equation, transformations, and operator expectation values in general form.
method: They derive the radial differential equation from the closed-form orbitals, verify solutions via power series and a Green's-function matrix formulation, and obtain closed-form expectation values and information measures.
result: New transformation relations to noninteger Slater-type orbitals are established, and general expressions for radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, Shannon entropy, and Fisher information are derived.
conclusion: The work extends the mathematical theory of Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers, but it is a specialized atomic-physics/mathematical chemistry contribution rather than a quantum information or thermodynamics result.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Statistical Watermarking For LLMs With Fixed And Optimizable Common Randomness
authors: Haiyun He, Yepeng Liu, Zhuoer Shen, Ziqiao Wang, Yongyi Mao, Yuheng Bu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of LLM-generated text, casting it as an independence test and characterizing fundamental limits under fixed and optimizable common randomness.
motivation: Existing LLM watermarking work is largely empirical and lacks a fundamental understanding of performance limits, motivating a unified theoretical treatment.
method: The authors formulate watermark embedding and detection as an independence test between generated text and common randomness, jointly designing embedder and detector while controlling worst-case false positive rate and text distortion.
result: They show that optimizing common randomness does not improve fundamental limits compared with fixed common randomness, but it can simplify detector design and enable a fixed, deterministic, model-agnostic optimal detector.
conclusion: Common randomness design is theoretically non-essential for optimal limits but practically valuable for detector simplicity, with quantified gaps for fixed uniform randomness and deterministic detectors.

title: Observables And Symmetries In Causal Fermion System
authors: Patrick Fischer, Claudio F. Paganini, Sahil Yadav
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.
tldr: The paper studies how observables and symmetries are related in causal fermion systems, with emphasis on position observables, spacetime isometries, and static Heisenberg-type evolution.
motivation: Causal fermion systems provide a foundational framework aimed at unifying spacetime and quantum theory, and the authors seek to clarify how geometric symmetries induce unitary symmetries and how observables behave under them.
method: The authors analyze covariance of position observables under unitary symmetries, derive Heisenberg-type evolution for static causal fermion systems, and establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of causal fermion systems built from Dirac equation solutions.
result: They show that position observables transform covariantly, obtain static Heisenberg evolution, and identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian in static spacetimes via the Dirac equation.
conclusion: The results provide a geometric and algebraic link between spacetime isometries and symmetries in causal fermion systems, but the work is foundational mathematical physics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universal Statistics Of Random Waves In Multi-Port non-Hermitian Scattering Systems
authors: Nadav Shaibe, Jared Erb, Steven M. Anlage
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the statistical properties of wave transport of a fixed multi-port non-Hermitian scattering system through wavefront shaping to explore all possible coherent illumination conditions. This is a departure from traditional approaches utilizing cavity shaping to create an ensemble of systems with different detailed scattering arrangements that lead to uncorrelated field configurations. Using microwave measurements in the low channel-number limit, we empirically demonstrate universal statistics in the probability density functions (PDF) of reflectivity, transmissivity, and absorptivity, Fisher information and the difference between forward propagating and time reversed transmissivity. Because the PDFs depend only on the number of input channels and the eigenvalues of Hermitian operators, we demonstrate how cavity shaping can be used to manipulate these eigenvalues, even creating Diabolic Point degeneracies, giving us direct control over the shapes and bounds of transport phenomena PDFs. We further investigate the PDFs when the excitations are finite bandwidth pulses as opposed to monochromatic waves, and determine the behavior in the limits of two channels and many channels. Our results establish a new paradigm in statistical investigations and cavity shaping applications by focusing on outcomes arising from all possible excitations, rather than creating conditions for one specific wavefront that optimally achieves a desired purpose.
tldr: The paper experimentally and theoretically studies universal statistical distributions of transport quantities in multi-port non-Hermitian scattering systems under all possible wavefront-shaping illumination conditions.
motivation: Traditional random-wave studies ensemble over cavity shapes to obtain uncorrelated scattering configurations; this work instead explores all coherent illumination conditions of a fixed system to establish universal statistics.
method: Microwave measurements in the low-channel-number limit are used to characterize probability density functions of reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, Fisher information, and forward versus time-reversed transmissivity, with cavity shaping employed to manipulate relevant Hermitian-operator eigenvalues.
result: The authors empirically demonstrate universal PDFs depending only on channel number and Hermitian-operator eigenvalues, show control over PDF shapes and bounds via engineered degeneracies including diabolic points, and analyze finite-bandwidth pulse and asymptotic channel limits.
conclusion: The work proposes a new paradigm for statistical wave-transport investigations and cavity-shaping applications by considering outcomes over all possible excitations rather than optimizing a single wavefront.

title: Femtosecond Free-Space Time-Frequency Transfer At Km/s Relative Motion With Doppler Compensation
authors: Jian-Yu Guan, Qi Shen, Lei Hou, Jin-Jian Han, Shen Zhang, Feng-Heng Che, Yi-Cheng Zhang, Shi Chen, Yao-Dong Hu, Zhi-Kang Qian, Yong Wang, Min Li, Shao-Mao Wang, Dan-Yang Zhu, Fa-Xi Chen, Li-Bo Li, Esamdin Ali, Ji-Gang Ren, Juan Yin, Rong Shu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Hai-Feng Jiang, Qiang Zhang, Jian-Wei Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A global optical clock network holds great promise for a wide range of applications, including international metrology--particularly the redefinition of the ``second''--as well as navigation, geoscience, and fundamental physics. Satellite-based high-precision time-frequency dissemination is essential for realizing such a network. Despite remarkable progress in ground-based free-space simulations over high-loss channels, the Doppler effect arising from satellite motion has remained an unsolved barrier. Here we demonstrate femtosecond two-way time-frequency transfer over a 113-km free-space link under simulated Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s. To overcome the Doppler barrier, we first reproduce satellite-like Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s on the ground by locking a frequency comb to a broadly tunable laser. We then correct the resulting disturbances with two complementary techniques: a dual-channel sampling architecture that compensates for optical dispersion and radio frequency (RF) nonlinearity while eliminating Nyquist dead zones, and an iterative interferogram reconstruction algorithm that removes Doppler-induced distortion. After correction, residual systematic errors are within [MATH] fs over the full 1.55 km/s range. Using simulated medium earth orbit (MEO) and geosynchronous orbit (GSO) satellite trajectories, we achieve fractional frequency instability of [MATH] at 4,600 s and [MATH] at 23,600 s, respectively. This extends the operational velocity range by nearly two orders of magnitude beyond previous free-space demonstrations, removing the last major technical barrier to a global femtosecond-precision satellite-based time-frequency link.
tldr: Demonstrates femtosecond two-way free-space time-frequency transfer over 113 km with Doppler compensation for simulated satellite motion up to 1.55 km/s.
motivation: Global optical clock networks require satellite-based high-precision time-frequency dissemination, but Doppler effects from satellite motion have remained a major barrier.
method: The authors simulate satellite-like Doppler shifts by locking a frequency comb to a tunable laser, then apply a dual-channel sampling architecture and an iterative interferogram reconstruction algorithm to correct dispersion, RF nonlinearity, and Doppler-induced distortion.
result: Residual systematic errors are within femtoseconds over the full 1.55 km/s range, achieving fractional frequency instability of about 1e-18 at 4,600 s for MEO and 23,600 s for GSO trajectories.
conclusion: This extends the operational velocity range by nearly two orders of magnitude and removes a key technical barrier for global femtosecond-precision satellite time-frequency links.

title: Quaternionic Wave Numbers And The Dirac Equation: Resolving The Nielsen--Ninomiya Barrier And Infinities
authors: Terence R. Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exemplify the applicability of the rational wave numbers by formulating the relativistic Dirac equation on the discrete sequence space [MATH] over the quaternions [MATH] and demonstrating how this resolves fundamental issues relating to Dirac's equation. Generating [MATH] from the primitive basis [MATH] as both a static closure and a dynamic enumeration, we show that coupling local quantum kinematics with global cosmological expansion leads to the following results: (1) Dirac 4-spinors and the Clifford algebra [MATH] emerge from the second Cayley--Dickson doubling (biquaternions [MATH]); (2) under dynamic generation on an integer clock lattice with causal horizon [MATH], relativistic difference operators require temporal depth, establishing clock beat [MATH] as the universal Matter Genesis Threshold; (3) the Nielsen--Ninomiya fermion doubling barrier is circumvented on modular sequences [MATH] because candidate zone-edge doubler modes ([MATH]) are actively pruned at the generational boundary by the coprime sieve projector [MATH] ([MATH]), preserving exact chiral symmetry without Wilson terms; (4) the discrete fermionic Green's function [MATH] possesses no coincident-point singularity ([MATH]), converting ultraviolet loop integrals into finite Dedekind and Kloosterman character sums, realizing Dirac's demand for an infinity-free theory; and (5) Zitterbewegung is resolved as an observable stroboscopic beat against vacuum reference [MATH], identifying rest mass [MATH] as a vacuum coupling beat frequency for stationary periodic cycles on the saturated quotient graph.
tldr: The paper proposes a quaternionic discrete formulation of the Dirac equation to evade Nielsen-Ninomiya fermion doubling and ultraviolet infinities.
motivation: It aims to resolve long-standing foundational issues in lattice Dirac theory, including fermion doubling, chiral symmetry, and ultraviolet divergences, by using rational wave numbers on a quaternionic sequence space.
method: The author constructs the Dirac equation on discrete sequence spaces over quaternions, generates the lattice dynamically with a causal horizon, and uses a coprime sieve projector to prune doubler modes.
result: The formulation yields emergent Dirac spinors and Clifford algebra, avoids the Nielsen-Ninomiya barrier without Wilson terms, converts loop integrals into finite character sums, and interprets rest mass as a vacuum coupling beat frequency.
conclusion: The work claims an infinity-free discrete Dirac theory and a new interpretation of Zitterbewegung and mass, but it is not aligned with quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Global Lanczos With Stochastic Error Correction For Trace Estimation Of Matrix Functions
authors: Michele Rinelli, Igor Simunec, Robbe Vermeiren
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new method for computing the trace of a matrix function [MATH], where [MATH] is a large, sparse, symmetric matrix. Our approach combines a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic correction of its error. Starting the global Lanczos process with the identity matrix yields a direct approximation of the trace through a small tridiagonal matrix. The resulting basis matrices are polynomials in [MATH], allowing the process to be implemented using sparse matrix-matrix multiplications when low-degree polynomials in [MATH] have moderate fill-in. However, increased fill-in may limit the number of iterations that can be performed efficiently. To address this limitation, we derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic estimator to the remainder. Even a moderately accurate estimate can substantially improve the accuracy, combining the deterministic method with the rapid initial convergence of stochastic trace estimators. We discuss error bounds and variance reduction, and present numerical experiments that compare the resulting method with existing ones.
tldr: The authors combine a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic estimator for the residual error to compute traces of large sparse matrix functions more accurately.
motivation: Global Lanczos with the identity start matrix gives a cheap deterministic trace estimate, but growing fill-in of the polynomial basis matrices limits the number of iterations, so the approximation saturates; a cheap correction of the remainder is therefore desirable.
method: They derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic trace estimator (Hutchinson-type) to that remainder, with analysis of error bounds and variance reduction.
result: Numerical experiments show that even a moderately accurate stochastic estimate of the remainder substantially improves accuracy over the purely deterministic global Lanczos method and competes with existing trace estimators.
conclusion: Hybridizing deterministic Krylov quadrature with stochastic remainder estimation yields a practical, accurate trace estimator for matrix functions of large sparse symmetric matrices.

title: Spacer-Engineered Spectral Selectivity In Metal-Carbon Solar-Thermal Absorbers
authors: X. Romain, A. P. Vafa, M. Florescu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectrally selective solar-thermal absorbers must capture sunlight while limiting emission at operating temperatures where the Planck spectrum overlaps the solar band. We connect this trade-off to a controlled optical mechanism in a metal-carbon metasurface. A radiative-limit calculation using AM1.5D illumination identifies how cutoff wavelength, infrared absorptivity and concentration together constrain equilibrium temperature, while the metasurface calculations reveal the additional role of a sharp spectral transition. We then separate the dielectric gap from the absorbing carbon layer in a gold--carbon architecture. Frequency-domain fields and material-resolved dissipation show that the spacer controls the overlap of a gap-localised mode with carbon, extending the high-absorptivity band and sharpening its infrared roll-off. A thickness sweep demonstrates that the spectrum with the strongest visible absorption need not give the highest radiative-limit equilibrium temperature. Polar-angle- and polarisation-resolved calculations demonstrate the angular robustness of the proposed plasmonic metasurface and assess the extent to which normal-incidence spectra approximate hemispherical emission. The calculated high-temperature values are benchmarks for the fixed-geometry, fixed-optical-constant model, not operating temperature predictions for the gold structure. The study establishes spacer-controlled loss partitioning as a route to shaping solar-thermal spectra and distinguishes optical selectivity from materials durability and useful heat output.
tldr: The paper designs and analyzes a gold-carbon plasmonic metasurface for spectrally selective solar-thermal absorption, linking spacer-controlled mode overlap to radiative-limit equilibrium temperature.
motivation: Spectrally selective solar-thermal absorbers must absorb sunlight while suppressing infrared emission, and the authors aim to connect this trade-off to a controlled optical mechanism in a metal-carbon metasurface.
method: The authors perform radiative-limit calculations under AM1.5D illumination and frequency-domain metasurface calculations, including material-resolved dissipation and thickness, angle, and polarization sweeps.
result: The spacer layer controls the overlap of a gap-localized mode with the carbon absorber, extending the high-absorptivity visible band and sharpening the infrared roll-off, though the strongest visible absorption does not necessarily maximize the radiative-limit equilibrium temperature.
conclusion: Spacer-controlled loss partitioning is established as a route to shaping solar-thermal spectra, while distinguishing optical selectivity from materials durability and useful heat output.

title: Predicting Local Electric Field In Al$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N P-i-n Photodiodes Using Exciton Franz-Keldysh Photocurrent Spectroscopy
authors: Himel Kundu Utsha, Manjur Muntasir, Md. Mohsinur Rahman Adnan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In AlGaN p-i-n photodiodes, reverse bias redshifts and broadens the sub-bandgap photocurrent responsivity through the eXciton Franz-Keldysh (XFK) effect, and this spectral line shape encodes the local electric field inside the device. Fitting the photocurrent spectra of two such photodiodes, with 5% and 40% Al, to an XFK absorption model at each bias yields the local voltage, [MATH], a single parameter that sets the line shape and uniquely determines the electric-field profile inside the device. In both devices, [MATH] varies linearly with the applied bias ([MATH] and [MATH]) but changes far more slowly than the bias itself, revealing a strong local reduction of the electric field that points to non-uniform electrostatics. The slopes show that only 12.4% of the applied bias in the 5% Al device, and 45.8% in the 40% Al device, drops across the junction at the probed location. Extrapolated to zero bias, [MATH] gives built-in voltages of 3.39 and 4.29 V, within 0.02 V of the 3.41 and 4.28 V obtained from technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, which validates the extracted local voltages at equilibrium. These results extend sub-bandgap photocurrent spectroscopy to AlGaN devices as an optical probe of local electrostatics, relevant to ultraviolet photodetectors and high-voltage electronics.
tldr: The paper extracts local electric fields in AlGaN p-i-n photodiodes by fitting sub-bandgap photocurrent spectra to an exciton Franz-Keldysh absorption model.
motivation: Local electrostatics in AlGaN photodiodes are important for ultraviolet photodetectors and high-voltage electronics but are difficult to probe directly.
method: Photocurrent spectra at varying reverse bias for devices with 5% and 40% Al are fitted to an XFK absorption model, yielding a local voltage parameter that determines the field profile.
result: The extracted local voltage varies linearly with applied bias but much more slowly than the bias, indicating non-uniform electrostatics; zero-bias extrapolation gives built-in voltages within 0.02 V of TCAD simulation.
conclusion: Sub-bandgap photocurrent spectroscopy is demonstrated as an optical probe of local electric fields in AlGaN devices, with potential relevance to UV photodetectors and power electronics.

title: Invariant Measures With Uniform Projection On Surfaces And Billiards
authors: Xiaolong Han
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space. As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium. In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.
tldr: The paper proves that Liouville measure is the unique geodesic-flow-invariant probability measure with normalized Riemannian volume projection on finite-area ergodic surfaces, and derives analogous results for ergodic planar billiards.
motivation: The work addresses the Katok-Knieper-Weiss conjecture in dimension two and connects invariant measures with phase-space versus physical-space equidistribution of high-energy Laplacian eigenfunctions.
method: The proof combines Fourier analysis in the fibers of the unit tangent bundle with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space, and treats billiards via related ergodic-theoretic techniques.
result: It establishes uniqueness of Liouville measure in the stated settings, obtains an entropy bound in higher dimensions, and shows that on such surfaces and the Bunimovich stadium, phase-space equidistribution is equivalent to physical-space equidistribution; this yields a new proof of scarring for almost every stadium.
conclusion: The paper resolves a two-dimensional case of the Katok-Knieper-Weiss conjecture and provides consequences for quantum ergodicity and scarring, while also constructing counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

title: Surrogate Symbols In Wireless Communications
authors: Zekeriya Uykan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Co-channel interference (CCI), caused by the inevitable aggressive channel reuse in dense deployments, remains a critical bottleneck for current and future wireless communication systems. In this paper, we address this bottleneck in an N-co-channel wireless communications network of single-antenna transmitters and receivers. The limiting case of this problem leads to a novel "thought experiment": If each receiver's own desired channel link is simultaneously completely blocked, can a Maximum Likelihood Detection at each receiver still recover its transmitted symbol? In the traditional way of thinking, the answer is no: The receiver obtains nothing but co-channel interference (CCI) plus thermal noise, and a receiver-side phase rotation cannot help, since there is no desired signal to align. Given only the channel matrix H -- and no knowledge of the transmitted symbols -- can the transmitters' phases be chosen so that the received signal becomes "almost" the desired symbol at every receiver? We show that the answer is yes. We first develop the underlying framework for the general case (nonzero own-channel link case), turning classical co-channel systems into a novel discrete phase-optimization problem, "Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization", and present two algorithms, "Minimum Phased-Interference Power algorithm (MiPIP)" and "Maximum Phased-Interference Support (MaPRIS)". We then show that the MaPRIS resolves the thought experiment: it converts hostile CCI into an "almost" desired symbol even when the own desired channel link is zero, yielding the counter-intuitive result that higher CCI variance yields higher SINR. Extensive simulation results confirm the findings. The gain promised by the proposed algorithms comes on top of any other CCI reduction techniques as our framework here is based on a bottom-line baseband model.
tldr: The paper proposes a discrete phase-optimization framework and two algorithms to mitigate co-channel interference in wireless networks, including a counterintuitive result where higher interference variance can improve SINR.
motivation: Co-channel interference is a critical bottleneck in dense wireless deployments, and conventional methods fail when the desired channel link is completely blocked.
method: The authors formulate the problem as 'Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization' and introduce the MiPIP and MaPRIS algorithms to choose transmitter phases based only on the channel matrix, aiming to make the received signal approximate the desired symbol via maximum likelihood detection.
result: MaPRIS resolves the thought experiment by converting hostile co-channel interference into an almost-desired symbol even with zero desired channel link, yielding higher SINR with higher interference variance in simulations.
conclusion: The proposed phase-optimization framework provides a bottom-line baseband solution that can complement existing CCI reduction techniques, with extensive simulations confirming the findings.

title: Spherical Functions Of The Quantum Symmetric Pair Of Type Fii
authors: Shaolong Han
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.
tldr: The paper proves Schlösser's conjecture identifying quantum FII spherical functions with Askey–Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and derives the associated radial operator.
motivation: Spherical functions of quantum symmetric pairs generalize zonal spherical functions, and their explicit connection to classical orthogonal polynomials (Askey–Wilson) is a structural question in the theory of quantum groups and coideal subalgebras.
method: Representation-theoretic and special-function techniques: analysis of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII, comparison of the radial part of the Casimir/Laplace operator with the Askey–Wilson difference operator, plus an explicit transport formula for shifted restrictions.
result: Schlösser's conjecture is established for equal left and right coideal parameters, the radial operator is determined explicitly, and a transport formula gives shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.
conclusion: The work settles a structural identification in quantum symmetric pair theory and extends it beyond the equal-parameter case, contributing to the harmonic analysis of quantum homogeneous spaces.

title: Quantifying Membership Inference Risks In Genomic Data Sharing: The Role Of Attacker's Auxiliary Information
authors: Maryam Ghasemian, Lynette Hammond Gerido, Erman Ayday
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Genomic data sharing is essential for biomedical research but introduces significant privacy risks, including membership inference attacks, in which an adversary determines whether a specific individual's data was used in a study. Existing privacy protections are typically applied after a release format has already been chosen, leaving researchers without a principled method to assess dataset-specific risk beforehand. We propose a server-assisted, principal component analysis-based pre-release auditing framework that maps genomic data into a shared low-dimensional space, applies epsilon-local differential privacy via the Laplace mechanism with a formally derived sensitivity for principal component analysis scores, and estimates membership inference attack power at a controlled 5% false-positive rate using a distance-threshold attack. A membership-neutrality diagnostic based on Unbiased Reconstruction Robustness is reported alongside attack power, precision, and recall.
