Experiments using the openSNP and 1000 Genomes Project datasets across multiple dimensionalities and privacy budgets show that separation between the researcher's dataset and public auxiliary data in principal component analysis space is a dominant determinant of attack success, exceeding the effect of perturbation level alone. Comparison against a genome-wide association study-style likelihood ratio test baseline further contextualizes the measured risk. This framework enables researchers, data repositories, and institutional review bodies to quantify dataset-specific membership inference risk before genomic data publication, supporting more informed and privacy-aware biomedical data-sharing decisions.
tldr: The paper proposes a pre-release auditing framework to quantify membership inference risk in genomic data sharing under local differential privacy.
motivation: Genomic data sharing creates privacy risks, and existing protections are applied after release-format choices, leaving no principled pre-release risk assessment.
method: It maps genomic data into a PCA space, applies epsilon-local differential privacy via the Laplace mechanism with derived sensitivity, and estimates membership inference attack power using a distance-threshold attack at a 5% false-positive rate.
result: Experiments on openSNP and 1000 Genomes show that separation between the dataset and public auxiliary data in PCA space dominates attack success more than perturbation level alone.
conclusion: The framework helps researchers and repositories quantify dataset-specific membership inference risk before genomic data publication.

title: Towards Self-Organizing Channel Coding In 6G-Enabled IoT Networks: Trends, Cognitive Architectures, And Open Challenges
authors: M. Moazam Azeem, Adil Raja, Ayaz Ahmad
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) of wireless communication is designed to facilitate distributed edge intelligence, ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), and massive machine-type communications (mMTC), all of which have the potential to revolutionize the Internet of Things (IoT). Autonomous vehicles, swarm robotics, XR, and industrial automation are IoT-centric 6G applications with demanding requirements; developing efficient, adaptive, and reliable channel coding methods is crucial to realizing this goal. This study explores the adaptation of various channel coding schemes to distributed IoT scenarios in 6G networks, covering both established and developing schemes, including LDPC, Turbo, Polar, and Fountain codes. We evaluate the relevance of recent developments to decentralized IoT designs, including AIassisted cognitive coding, neural network-based decoding, adaptive and context-aware coding, quantum and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) coding. We further propose CACADe-6G, a cognitive architecture for adaptive channel coding; our evaluation shows that its principal benefit over simpler adaptive baselines lies in reduced switching overhead and energy consumption, rather than a guaranteed reduction in bit error rate relative to a memoryless threshold comparator. We compare different channel coding schemes with respect to latency, energy, and reliability requirements, and highlight important use cases. Findings from this study reveal current research gaps and identify potential future directions for coding in intelligent, large-scale IoT systems, aiming to guide future research and support the deployment of 6G-enabled IoT technologies.
tldr: This paper reviews channel coding schemes for 6G-enabled IoT networks and proposes a cognitive architecture, CACADe-6G, for adaptive coding selection.
motivation: 6G IoT applications require efficient, adaptive, and reliable channel coding, particularly in distributed edge scenarios with demanding latency, energy, and reliability constraints.
method: The authors survey LDPC, Turbo, Polar, and Fountain codes for decentralized IoT designs, discuss AI-assisted and RIS-related coding trends, and introduce CACADe-6G, a cognitive adaptive coding architecture.
result: The proposed architecture primarily reduces switching overhead and energy consumption relative to simpler adaptive baselines, rather than guaranteeing lower bit error rate than a memoryless threshold comparator.
conclusion: The study identifies research gaps and future directions for self-organizing channel coding in large-scale intelligent IoT systems, with the goal of supporting 6G deployment.

title: Bringing Coherent Closer To Compute: Coherent-lite Multidimensional On-chip Interconnect Beyond 100 Terabits Per Second
authors: Yongzhu Hu, Aolong Sun, Huayuan Qin, An Yan, Jialin He, Yuqin Yuan, Junhao Zhao, Chao Shen, Ziwei Li, Peng Sun, Hui Chen, Chao Li, Xu Zhang, Bowei Dong, Zhixue He, Nan Chi, Shaohua Yu, Junwen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continued scaling of artificial intelligence (AI) demands optical interconnects that deliver higher bandwidth density within stringent electrical-bandwidth and energy budgets. Coherent optics offers a route beyond the per-lane bandwidth constraints of intensity-modulation direct-detection links, yet its receiver complexity and power overhead have largely confined its use to longer reaches. Here we bring coherent optics closer to compute by demonstrating a coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip interconnect that combines wavelength- and mode-division multiplexing with self-homodyne detection. The architecture co-transmits the local oscillator (LO) and parallel data channels within a single silicon waveguide, using polarization-division routing to preserve LO purity and support high-order modulation. Based on this principle, we develop an inverse-designed dual-polarization mode multiplexer that provides over 37 dB inter-polarization isolation across the C band in an [MATH]m[MATH] footprint, enabling millimetre-scale on-chip multimode routing. Without power-intensive digital carrier recovery, the architecture delivers a single-wavelength line rate of 2 Tb s[MATH] and scales to an aggregate line rate of 103.96 Tb s[MATH] across four modes and 100 wavelengths, using formats up to 64-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). These results extend on-chip coherent interconnects into the hundred-terabit-per-second regime, offering a scalable route to bandwidth-dense optical connectivity for next-generation computing systems.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip optical interconnect using self-homodyne detection, wavelength- and mode-division multiplexing, achieving 103.96 Tb/s aggregate line rate.
motivation: AI and computing systems require higher-bandwidth, energy-efficient optical interconnects beyond intensity-modulation direct-detection limits, while coherent optics has been too complex and power-hungry for short-reach on-chip use.
method: The authors co-transmit a local oscillator and parallel data channels in a single silicon waveguide, use polarization-division routing for LO purity, and develop an inverse-designed dual-polarization mode multiplexer with >37 dB isolation.
result: The architecture achieves 2 Tb/s per wavelength and 103.96 Tb/s aggregate across four modes and 100 wavelengths using up to 64-QAM without power-intensive digital carrier recovery.
conclusion: This extends on-chip coherent interconnects into the hundred-terabit-per-second regime and offers a scalable path for bandwidth-dense optical connectivity in next-generation computing.

title: Privacy-Preserving Clustering Algorithm And Parameter Selection For Collaborative Population Stratification Using Distributed Pca
authors: Maryam Ghasemian, Lynette Hammond Gerido, Erman Ayday
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a privacy-preserving selection layer for collaborative population stratification workflows, enabling an honest-but-curious server to recommend a strong clustering algorithm-hyperparameter configuration from privacy protected shares. Instead of using a fixed workflow such as PCA followed by K-Means with a preset number of clusters, the framework compares multiple clustering methods and parameter settings under privacy constraints. To avoid relying on a public reference basis, we construct a shared low-dimensional representation through a distributed-PCA (DPCA) procedure in which each party computes local top-[MATH] principal-component information and the server aggregates only low-rank summaries to recover a global basis. Building on this representation, the framework supports three LDP-protected pipelines: PCA then Noise, Noise then PCA, and Noise-Only. The server evaluates clustering methods and parameter settings using internal validation metrics and recommends a top-performing configuration from the perturbed data; this step is pure post-processing. Experiments on openSNP and 1000 Genomes show that the server-side selection layer reliably identifies strong settings from LDP-protected data. Across both datasets, the PCA-based pipelines outperform Noise-Only in clustering utility, communication cost, and runtime, and show lower membership-inference attack (MIA) power at small privacy budgets. Overall, they provide the best utility--scalability trade-off in our setting.
tldr: The paper proposes a privacy-preserving selection layer that recommends clustering algorithms and hyperparameters from local-differential-privacy (LDP) protected data using a distributed PCA representation for collaborative population stratification.
motivation: Collaborative genomic analyses across institutions require population stratification, but centralized workflows and fixed PCA+K-Means pipelines leak information and may be suboptimal under privacy constraints.
method: Each party computes local top principal components, a server aggregates low-rank summaries to recover a global basis, and three LDP-protected pipelines (PCA-then-Noise, Noise-then-PCA, Noise-Only) are compared using internal validation metrics as pure post-processing.
result: On openSNP and 1000 Genomes, PCA-based pipelines outperformed Noise-Only in clustering utility, communication cost and runtime, and showed lower membership-inference attack power at small privacy budgets.
conclusion: The server-side selection layer reliably identifies strong clustering configurations from LDP-protected data, offering the best utility-scalability trade-off in this setting.

title: An Analytic Two-Dimensional Benchmark For Integrated Autocorrelation Times In Branching Monte Carlo Part Ii: Operator Estimation From Functional Expansion Tallies
authors: Jilang Miao, Guillaume L. Giudicelli, William Reed Kendrick
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional expansion tallies can represent transport operators for Monte Carlo correlation prediction without first constructing a fine cell transition matrix. We tally Galerkin operators directly from birth-to-absorption histories, retaining the sampled departure measure through an empirical mass matrix. Operator moments and an estimated offspring second moment give branching autocorrelations and integrated autocorrelation times without an eigendecomposition. The analytic benchmark from Part I supplies continuum and noise-free finite-model references. At the compared sizes, cosine and Legendre models have smaller IACT errors and require less operator storage than the cell model, and the branching reweighting reduces their representation error by a further factor near five while leaving the cell error unchanged. The measured runtime benefit is basis dependent. Profiling separates shared transport from the additional costs of operator assembly and prediction.
tldr: The paper develops Galerkin functional-expansion tallies for estimating branching Monte Carlo transport operators and their integrated autocorrelation times without building fine cell transition matrices, benchmarked against an analytic two-dimensional reference.
motivation: Monte Carlo transport codes need accurate autocorrelation estimates for correlation prediction and variance assessment, but constructing fine cell transition matrices is prohibitively expensive and noisy.
method: Galerkin operators are tallied directly from birth-to-absorption histories using cosine and Legendre bases, with an empirical mass matrix retaining the departure measure; operator moments and an offspring second moment yield branching autocorrelations and IACTs without eigendecomposition, validated against the analytic benchmark from Part I.
result: Cosine and Legendre models show smaller IACT errors and lower operator storage than the cell model at the tested sizes, and branching reweighting reduces representation error by roughly a factor of five for the spectral bases while leaving the cell model's error unchanged; runtime benefits are basis dependent.
conclusion: Functional expansion tallies offer an efficient, basis-dependent alternative to cell-based transition matrices for autocorrelation estimation in branching Monte Carlo, with profiling separating shared transport cost from operator assembly and prediction overhead.

title: Gravitational And Maxwell--Proca-Type Structures In A Variational Metric-Affine Framework
authors: Old\v{r}ich Stol\'in
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Einstein's nonsymmetric metric-affine Lagrangian density with a generally nonsymmetric metric and an affine connection treated as independent variational variables. The resulting connection equation belongs to the classical Einstein--Hlavat\'y--Tonnelat framework, while the unrestricted metric Euler--Lagrange equation is analyzed without a divergence constraint on the antisymmetric metric density. Its symmetric part takes the form of Einstein-type gravitational equations with geometrically induced source terms and reduces to the vacuum Einstein equations in the torsion-free limit. The antisymmetric part becomes a geometric constitutive relation based on the irreducible decomposition of torsion. Its contracted four-divergence yields a general vector-field equation with geometric source and response terms. Under a trace--axial reduction, [MATH] gives a source-free Maxwell-type equation, whereas constant nonzero [MATH] gives a Proca-type equation. Independently, a trace of the generalized Bianchi identities yields the homogeneous Maxwell-type pair associated with the torsion trace, while the connection equation implies a Lorenz-type condition. Thus gravitational, constitutive, Maxwell--Proca-type, and Lorenz-type structures arise as compatible consequences of one metric-affine variational system. The antisymmetric dynamical level is generated by the contracted four-divergence of its constitutive level. No independent electromagnetic or matter field is introduced.
tldr: A purely classical metric-affine variational study showing that gravitational, constitutive, Maxwell- and Proca-type, and Lorenz-type structures emerge jointly from Einstein's nonsymmetric Lagrangian.
motivation: The author aims to show that electromagnetic-looking structures can arise geometrically from a nonsymmetric metric-affine Lagrangian without introducing an independent electromagnetic or matter field.
method: Variational treatment of Einstein's nonsymmetric metric-affine Lagrangian with independent nonsymmetric metric and affine connection, analyzing the metric and connection Euler-Lagrange equations, irreducible torsion decomposition, and traces of generalized Bianchi identities.
result: The symmetric metric equation reduces to Einstein-type equations (vacuum Einstein in the torsion-free limit), while the contracted four-divergence of the antisymmetric constitutive relation yields Maxwell-type equations under a trace-axial reduction and Proca-type equations for constant nonzero trace, alongside a Lorenz-type condition from the connection equation.
conclusion: Gravitational, constitutive, and Maxwell-Proca-type structures appear as compatible consequences of a single classical metric-affine variational system, with no independent electromagnetic field assumed.

title: Beyond Global Density In A Stochastic Sandpile: The Role Of Spatial Signatures In The Predictability Of Extremes
authors: Kamil P. Orzechowski, Julian Sienkiewicz, Piotr Fronczak
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In self-organized critical systems the global load is a strong precursor of extreme events. In the two-dimensional Manna sandpile, grain density alone predicts extreme avalanches with an AUC of about 0.96. We ask whether density fully determines the system's readiness for an extreme event, that is, whether microstates with the same number of grains are equivalent. Because density is such a strong predictor, a method that sees the full microstate can score well just by counting grains. We therefore compare only states with an identical number of grains. Even then, both a parameter-free statistic and a convolutional network distinguish states that precede an extreme avalanche from typical ones, while shuffled controls do not. The signal is a load contrast between the center and the dissipative boundaries, carried by the two lowest symmetric cosine modes. Their normalized energy is a single variable that needs no training. Together with density it recovers most of the gain that a network trained on the full microstate achieves over density alone. Readiness for an extreme avalanche therefore depends both on the total load and on how that load is distributed relative to the boundaries.
tldr: The paper studies whether grain density alone determines readiness for extreme avalanches in the 2D Manna sandpile, finding that spatial load distribution relative to boundaries provides additional predictive signal.
motivation: In self-organized critical systems, global load strongly predicts extreme events, but it is unclear whether microstates with identical grain number are equally close to an extreme avalanche.
method: The authors compare only sandpile states with identical total grain number, using a parameter-free spatial statistic and a convolutional network, with shuffled controls, to identify predictive microstate features.
result: States preceding extreme avalanches are distinguishable from typical same-density states; the signal is a center-boundary load contrast captured by the two lowest symmetric cosine modes, and combining this with density recovers most of the network's gain over density alone.
conclusion: Extreme-event readiness depends not only on total load but also on how that load is spatially distributed relative to dissipative boundaries.

title: A Las Vegas Algorithm For Satisfiable Sat Formulas, With An Application To Timetabling
authors: Fabio Dias
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many scheduling problems need many different feasible timetables, and a view of how much freedom each event has. We study a Las Vegas algorithm that samples satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula one variable at a time: it draws each value from an estimate of its conditional probability, propagates, and restarts on a contradiction. Every output is a checked solution and comes with the exact probability of producing it. We prove that a run succeeds with probability at least [MATH], where [MATH] is the expected Kullback--Leibler divergence between the true and estimated conditional probabilities along the run of a uniform solution. We also bound the distance of the outputs from uniform from the samples alone; it is a divergence in the opposite direction to [MATH], so a sampler can succeed more often while being farther from uniform. On generated timetabling instances counted exactly, belief propagation on the timetabling problem brings [MATH] to at most about one bit, and the estimated counts are within 2% of the exact ones. On a real university instance of the International Timetabling Competition 2019, rerunning only the failed runs delivered all 72 requested timetables with each of two estimators. Belief propagation succeeds in 31% of runs. Steered by a Markov chain that carries a nearly feasible timetable, it succeeds in 65% of runs, with outputs at least 300 bits from uniform. There the importance weights are too uneven to estimate the number of timetables, and we certify a lower bound instead. For random 3-SAT, an estimator whose [MATH] grows logarithmically would give a polynomial-time Las Vegas algorithm beyond the densities at which any algorithm is proved to succeed; we conjecture that one exists below the satisfiability threshold.
tldr: A classical Las Vegas sampling algorithm for satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas is developed and applied to university timetabling instances.
motivation: Scheduling and timetabling problems require generating many diverse feasible solutions and quantifying how much freedom each event has.
method: The algorithm samples satisfying assignments variable-by-variable using estimated conditional probabilities from belief propagation, propagates constraints, and restarts upon contradiction, giving exact output probabilities and KL-divergence-based success guarantees.
result: On generated timetabling instances belief propagation reduces the divergence to about one bit with counts within 2% of exact values, and on an ITC 2019 university instance all 72 requested timetables were obtained, with success rates of 31% (belief propagation) and 65% (Markov-chain steering).
conclusion: The approach provides certified sampling guarantees and practical timetabling performance, with conjectures about polynomial-time Las Vegas algorithms for random 3-SAT below the satisfiability threshold.

title: Spectral Conditioning Of Weighted Multivariate Vandermonde Operators Via Radial Beurling--Selberg Approximation
authors: Joseph Gabet, Maxime Ferreira Da Costa, Kiryung Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish explicit eigenvalue bounds for Gram matrices of weighted multivariate Vandermonde operators with separated nodes on a torus. The squared magnitudes of the weights are samples of a nonnegative radial spectral energy density whose profile has bounded variation, finite energy, and finite weighted variation cost; compact support is not required. The estimate holds in every dimension and depends on the periodic Euclidean separation and the weighted variation integral. For compactly supported profiles, our analysis combines a signed layer decomposition with the ball approximants of Holt and Vaaler; the noncompactly supported case follows by truncation. Combining the resulting radial envelopes with a bandlimited sampling identity based on Poisson summation yields the spectral bounds by eliminating off-diagonal interactions and nonzero diagonal aliases. The result covers nonmonotone profiles and discontinuous radial low-pass filters, and it is complemented by a global elementary upper bound on the Holt--Vaaler cost that exhibits two radial regimes.
tldr: The paper derives explicit eigenvalue bounds for Gram matrices of weighted multivariate Vandermonde operators with separated nodes on a torus using radial Beurling--Selberg approximation.
motivation: The authors aim to quantify spectral conditioning of weighted multivariate Vandermonde systems under general radial spectral energy densities, including noncompactly supported and nonmonotone profiles.
method: They combine signed layer decomposition, Holt--Vaaler ball approximants, truncation for noncompact support, and a bandlimited sampling identity based on Poisson summation to eliminate off-diagonal and aliasing contributions.
result: The analysis yields dimension-independent explicit spectral bounds depending on periodic Euclidean separation and a weighted variation integral, plus a global elementary upper bound on the Holt--Vaaler cost with two radial regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a general harmonic-analysis framework for spectral conditioning of Vandermonde operators, extending prior results to discontinuous and nonmonotone radial profiles without compact support.

title: Joint Channel Estimation, Data Detection, And Phase Noise Tracking In Massive Mimo Systems
authors: Duy H. N. Nguyen Toan-Van Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Communication over multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is degraded by phase noise (PN) arising from imperfect local oscillators, with PN becoming more severe at higher carrier frequencies. Existing methods either rely on linearized Kalman-filter approaches or apply variational Bayes (VB) only to individual stages, such as data detection under a static phase prior, or channel estimation alone, leaving no unified framework that tracks an evolving PN process consistently across pilot and data transmission. This paper develops such a framework for uplink massive MIMO. Specifically, we first propose VB-Tracking, which employs von Mises priors and coordinate-ascent VB inference to jointly estimate the channel and track the transmit and receive PN trajectories during the pilot phase without linearization. We then propose VB-Detecting for joint data detection and phase tracking by absorbing the transmit PN into a composite transmit variable. Using a sequentially propagated von Mises predictive prior, the composite variable admits an exact closed-form posterior. Finally, we propose VB-Refining, which periodically re-estimates the channel during data transmission using the soft posterior moments of reliably detected transmit symbols as virtual pilots. We show that VB-Detecting scales linearly in the number of users, receive antennas, constellation size, and iterations. Simulations against EKF-EP, EKF-ZF, and JED baselines show that VB-Tracking, VB-Detecting, and VB-Refining together achieve lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate, with the performance gap widening at high SNR and under severe PN.
tldr: A variational-Bayes framework for joint channel estimation, data detection, and phase-noise tracking in uplink massive MIMO systems.
motivation: Phase noise from imperfect local oscillators degrades MIMO communication and worsens at high carrier frequencies, while existing linearized Kalman-filter and stage-wise variational-Bayes methods fail to track an evolving phase-noise process consistently across pilot and data phases.
method: The authors propose VB-Tracking (von Mises priors with coordinate-ascent variational inference for joint channel estimation and transmit/receive phase tracking during pilots, without linearization), VB-Detecting (joint detection and phase tracking via a composite transmit variable with a sequentially propagated von Mises predictive prior admitting closed-form posteriors), and VB-Refining (periodic channel re-estimation using soft posterior moments of reliable symbols as virtual pilots).
result: VB-Detecting scales linearly in users, receive antennas, constellation size, and iterations, and simulations against EKF-EP, EKF-ZF, and JED baselines show lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate, with the gap widening at high SNR and severe phase noise.
conclusion: The unified variational-Bayes framework provides consistent phase-noise tracking across pilot and data transmission and outperforms existing baselines in massive MIMO uplink, though it lies entirely within classical wireless communications.

title: Interpolation, Factorization, And Approximation In The Numerical Radius Unit Ball
authors: Hamidul Ahmed, Mainak Bhowmik, B. Krishna Das, Haripada Sau
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as [MATH]-Schur functions. In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of [MATH]-Schur function [MATH] into a classical Schur function [MATH] and bounded holomorphic matrix functions [MATH] coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data. Finally, we introduce [MATH]-inner functions - [MATH]-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a [MATH]-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: [MATH]-inner functions are dense in the [MATH]-Schur class under the compact-open topology.
tldr: The paper develops Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions whose values lie in the numerical radius unit ball.
motivation: It aims to extend Schur-class interpolation from the operator-norm setting to the numerical-radius setting, where standard Pick-matrix positivity is insufficient.
method: The authors introduce numerical-radius Schur functions, use Ando's characterization, establish constructive factorization and dilation representations, and give a dual Nehari-type distance criterion.
result: They obtain necessary and sufficient solvability criteria for the interpolation problem and prove density of numerical-radius inner functions, yielding a Carathéodory approximation theorem.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic function-theoretic framework for numerical-radius contractions, but it is pure operator-theoretic analysis with no direct quantum information relevance.

title: Martingale And Signed Diffusive Optimal Transport: Geodesics And Gradient Flows
authors: Aymeric Baradat, Jean-David Benamou, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Vialard
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities [MATH] on the circle and a momentum [MATH] satisfy [MATH], and the cost of the path is the action [MATH]. The diffusivity [MATH] is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint [MATH] gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the [MATH]-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.
tldr: A mathematical paper on signed diffusive optimal transport on the circle and real line, establishing geodesics, Gamma-convergence of discrete schemes, and convergence of a modified JKO gradient flow to the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the martingale Benamou-Brenier framework of Huesmann-Trevisan by allowing the diffusivity to take either sign, thereby connecting optimal transport, martingale constraints, and fourth-order gradient flows.
method: They prove Gamma-convergence of time-discrete and fully discrete Fourier-grid problems, analyze a modified JKO scheme on the torus, and numerically compute geodesics and JKO trajectories via Douglas-Rachford splitting and an interior-point method with interval-arithmetic dual bounds.
result: Convergence to a weak solution of the one-dimensional DLSS equation is shown under a positive lower bound on densities along the scheme, and the limit of minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum is identified for smooth potentials.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous variational and numerical framework for signed diffusive transport, though it lies entirely within classical PDE/optimal-transport mathematics with no quantum information or quantum thermodynamic content.

title: An All-steps-at-once Algorithm For Time-domain Wave Propagation In Heterogeneous And Unbounded Media
authors: M. Ganesh V. Dom\'{\i}nguez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other. For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.
tldr: The paper develops a convolution-quadrature algorithm that solves transient acoustic wave propagation in heterogeneous unbounded media by reducing the evolution problem to a family of damped Helmholtz problems solved in parallel, with an overlapping FEM-BEM coupling discretization.
motivation: Transient wave propagation in unbounded heterogeneous media requires handling both spatial heterogeneity and an open exterior; the authors aim for a scheme where all time steps can be computed at once, in parallel, without mesh conformance to the heterogeneity or between the two discretizations.
method: Multistep convolution quadrature is applied to the time-domain solution operator, yielding independent Helmholtz problems at complex damped frequencies, which are discretized by FEM inside a bounding polygon and BEM on an enclosed smooth curve, with new explicit bounds on the solution operators in terms of the Laplace parameter and the wave speed.
result: The derived bounds give convergence of the A-stable time discretization, and estimates on exponential decay away from the heterogeneity show the BEM correction is small, needed only over a limited range of weakly damped frequencies, and cheap (a few GMRES iterations); numerical experiments confirm predicted time and space convergence rates.
conclusion: The CQ-based FEM-BEM coupling provides a provably convergent, fully parallelizable-in-time solver for transient acoustic scattering in heterogeneous unbounded media, with a cheap and localized exterior correction.

title: Stargate: Security Analysis And Mission-Aware Firewall For The CubeSat Space Protocol
authors: Owen Ramsey, Carlos Gonzalez-Cortes, Efren Lopez-Morales
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) is widely used for communication in CubeSat missions, yet its security model and attack surface remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present a systematic security analysis of CSP and identify fundamental limitations in its trust assumptions, coarse-grained network abstractions, privileged management services, application command semantics, and lack of mission-context awareness. Based on these findings, we develop a taxonomy of CSP attacks spanning four classes: network identity abuse, management service abuse, application semantic abuse, and mission context abuse. We then introduce Stargate, a modular, mission-aware firewall that enforces CSP-specific policies derived from this taxonomy, including node and service authorization, command-level filtering, and mission-context constraints. We implement Stargate and evaluate it on a virtual testbed based on a real-world CubeSat mission and flight software. Stargate successfully blocks all 11 representative attacks across the four attack classes while introducing only 1.42 ms of additional median round-trip latency. Our results demonstrate that protocol- and mission-aware policy enforcement provides a practical approach for securing CSP-based spacecraft networks.
tldr: The paper presents a security analysis of the CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) and proposes Stargate, a mission-aware firewall that blocks representative attacks with low latency.
motivation: CSP is widely used in CubeSat communications but its security model and attack surface are insufficiently understood, leaving spacecraft networks exposed.
method: The authors systematically analyze CSP trust assumptions and abstractions, build an attack taxonomy across four classes, and implement a modular firewall enforcing CSP-specific policies on a virtual testbed based on a real CubeSat mission.
result: Stargate blocks all 11 representative attacks across the four classes while adding only 1.42 ms of median round-trip latency.
conclusion: Protocol- and mission-aware policy enforcement offers a practical approach to securing CSP-based spacecraft networks.

title: On The Boomerang Spectrum Of The Apn Power Function $x^{q+2}$ Over $\F_{q^2}$
authors: Kirpa Garg, Constanza Riera, Pantelimon St\u{a}nic\u{a}
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the boomerang spectrum of the almost perfect nonlinear power function [MATH] over [MATH], where [MATH] is an odd prime power with [MATH]. The connection of Pal and Stnic between boomerang entries and [MATH]-differential entries reduces the problem to counting roots of a single equation. We determine the complete contribution from nonzero parameters in [MATH]. For parameters outside [MATH], we obtain a quintic over [MATH] in terms of the parameter's trace and norm, with a separate formula when the trace is zero. We exclude the entry four when [MATH] and characterize its occurrence when [MATH] through a repeated-root parametrization and a residual cubic. We also evaluate the first nonsubfield moment and an aggregate quadratic-character sum, and prove a Weil bound for each nonzero trace. Explicit secant and residual-cubic formulas express the second, third, and fourth falling-factorial moments as finite sums. Once the size-four frequency is known, these moments recover all remaining frequencies through a nonsingular five-dimensional system. A closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.
tldr: The paper computes the complete boomerang spectrum of the APN power function x^(q+2) over F_{q^2}, reducing the problem to counting roots of a quintic and related equations.
motivation: Boomerang and differential spectra of APN functions determine the resistance of block-cipher S-boxes to boomerang-style cryptanalysis, and the spectrum of x^(q+2) was previously only partially known.
method: Uses the Pal–Stanica connection between boomerang entries and c-differential entries to reduce the count to root counting of a single equation, then analyzes the resulting quintic over F_q in terms of trace and norm of the parameter, with a repeated-root parametrization and residual cubic for the entry four.
result: The contribution from nonzero parameters in F_q is fully determined; the first nonsubfield moment and an aggregate quadratic-character sum are evaluated with Weil bounds for each nonzero trace; falling-factorial moments up to order four are given as explicit finite sums, which recover all remaining frequencies via a nonsingular five-dimensional linear system once the size-four frequency is known.
conclusion: The boomerang spectrum is essentially determined up to the size-four frequency, but a closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.

title: Who Observes Whom: Network Rationalizability And Its Complexity
authors: Mohammadamin Fazli Mojtaba Fayaz-Bakhsh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.20110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nash equilibrium and rationalizability sit at opposite informational extremes: the former presumes that each player knows all opponents' strategies, the latter that players reason from common knowledge of rationality alone. When visibility is partial and asymmetric, we study the solution concepts induced by a directed [MATH] in which an edge [MATH] means that [MATH] observes [MATH]'s strategy. A set of profiles is if every profile in it can be justified, for every player, by conjectures from the same set that agree with everything the player observes. We consider conjectures (single profiles) and conjectures (distributions over profiles). Both range from Nash equilibrium on the complete network to point- and correlated rationalizability on the empty network, and shrink monotonically as links are added. Network topology governs both behavior and complexity. A predicted profile can be found in polynomial time on the empty network, whereas a single link makes search [MATH]-hard: under one-sided two-player monitoring, the observed player's strategies are exactly her Nash equilibrium strategies. On hierarchical networks (transitive tournaments), membership reduces recursively to smaller games and admits polynomial-size certificates, placing verification in [MATH], and in [MATH] for two players. On the directed three-cycle, however, iterated elimination may never terminate under either variant, and under point conjectures interior predictions may admit only infinite witness sets, a pathology that belief conjectures avoid in the same game. Finally, when only realized pure actions are observed, the solution set is guaranteed to be non-empty exactly when the network has no edges, and is computable in time [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies solution concepts for games with asymmetric partial strategy observability, characterizing network rationalizability and its computational complexity.
motivation: Nash equilibrium and rationalizability assume opposite informational extremes, and the authors aim to understand intermediate regimes where players observe only some opponents' strategies.
method: They define rationalizability relative to a directed observation network using point and belief conjectures, then analyze existence, monotonicity, and complexity on empty, single-link, hierarchical, cyclic, and realized-action networks.
result: The authors show polynomial-time prediction on the empty network, NP-hardness with a single link, recursive membership on transitive tournaments, possible nontermination on directed three-cycles, and a nonemptiness condition tied to having no edges when only realized actions are observed.
conclusion: Network topology sharply controls both strategic predictions and computational complexity, revealing pathologies and tractable special cases for partial-observability rationalizability.

title: All Edges Lead To Rome: Analyzing Late Antiquity Regime Shifts Using Coin Hoard Data
authors: Juan J. Merelo-Guerv\'os
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex network analysis and other statistical techniques can be fruitfully applied to historical data to understand dynamics that brought the territory under study to a certain state. In this paper we use the FLAME database to understand when a drastic change of trade regime occurred in the Italian peninsula by looking at mint-hoard links that are evidence of a physical connection between them. By using changepoint analysis to pinpoint precise dates in the time series of these links, and then historical as well as network data to establish the sequence of network collapse, we find that the demise of the Western Roman Empire started at the beginning of the 5th century AD, yielding a more precise sequence of how and when it reached Italia.
tldr: The paper applies complex network analysis and changepoint detection to Roman coin hoard data to date regime shifts in Late Antiquity Italy.
motivation: The author aims to use statistical and network techniques on historical mint-hoard data to better pinpoint when and how trade regime changes occurred during the decline of the Western Roman Empire.
method: The study uses the FLAME database to construct mint-hoard link networks and applies changepoint analysis to time series of these links, supplemented by historical and network data.
result: The analysis locates the start of the Western Roman Empire's demise at the beginning of the 5th century AD and proposes a more precise sequence of network collapse reaching Italia.
conclusion: Network-based changepoint analysis of coin hoard data can provide refined dating and sequencing of historical regime shifts, though the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Accelerating Atomistic-Continuum Simulations Of Multilayer 2d Materials With Functional Principal Component Analysis-Based Machine Learning
authors: Jonathan Oleson, Abhishek Keripale, Shashank Pathrudkar, Susanta Ghosh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomistic-continuum simulations of complex wrinkling deformations in large-area multilayer two-dimensional (2D) materials are computationally expensive. To accelerate these simulations, this work presents a machine-learning (ML) framework that first constructs a low-dimensional representation of the deformation field, then learns the deformation in this reduced space. Dimensionality reduction of deformed 2D membranes is challenging because of the extremely high dimensionality of discretized deformation fields, the need to preserve surface continuity and prescribed geometric constraints, the stochastic nature of wrinkling patterns, and the limited availability of training data. We address these challenges using two-dimensional functional principal component analysis (FPCA). The proposed FPCA representation reduces deformation fields containing millions of degrees of freedom to latent spaces with only tens of dimensions while preserving the continuity of the deformed surface. In addition, prescribed homogeneous boundary constraints are satisfied exactly through an appropriate choice of basis functions in the FPCA representation. A neural network is then trained to predict the principal components from the system and loading parameters. The resulting ML-predicted deformation fields are used as high-quality initial configurations for the atomistic-continuum solver, which subsequently performs energy minimization to obtain equilibrium solutions. The framework is demonstrated for multilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and combined biaxial compression and simple shear. For the most computationally intensive large-strain cases, the proposed approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8 times while converging to final energies comparable to, and in some cases lower than, those obtained using conventional atomistic-continuum initialization.
tldr: A machine-learning framework using functional principal component analysis accelerates atomistic-continuum simulations of wrinkling in multilayer 2D materials.
motivation: Atomistic-continuum simulations of large-area multilayer 2D materials with complex wrinkling deformations are computationally prohibitive, so a reduced-order surrogate is needed to speed up equilibrium solving.
method: Two-dimensional functional principal component analysis builds a low-dimensional, continuity-preserving representation of deformation fields with exactly satisfied boundary constraints, and a neural network maps system/loading parameters to principal components to generate initial configurations for energy minimization.
result: For multilayer graphene under uniaxial, biaxial, and combined biaxial-shear compression, the approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8x on the most intensive large-strain cases while reaching final energies comparable to or lower than conventional initialization.
conclusion: FPCA-based machine learning offers an effective route to accelerate atomistic-continuum simulations of 2D material wrinkling without sacrificing solution quality.

title: Higher-order Statistical Structure In Perfume Item Combinations Beyond A Pairwise Maximum-entropy Model
authors: Jun'ichi Ozaki Yohei Shida
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find that deviations from a pairwise maximum-entropy model in perfume item combinations are organized around particular shared item pairs. We analyze 1,979 perfumes using 50 binary variables representing the most frequently listed items. Although the pairwise model approximately reproduces the distribution of the number of listed items per perfume, the observed three-item marginal distributions exhibit deviations exceeding those obtained from synthetic datasets subjected to the same model-refitting procedure. Strongly deviating triplets are concentrated around shared item pairs, and this concentration cannot be explained by the participation frequencies of individual items alone. We then introduce three-body couplings for 50 selected triplets and reoptimize all model parameters. The sum of squared standardized residuals over the remaining 19,550 triplets decreases by 5.44\%, with substantially larger reductions for triplets sharing an item pair with selected triplets. Furthermore, a static linear-response calculation accounting for the readjustment of lower-order parameters approximately reproduces the resulting changes in predicted co-occurrence frequencies, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.850. These results reveal the organization of higher-order statistical dependencies and characterize how selected three-body couplings affect predictions throughout the system.
tldr: A statistical-physics analysis of 1,979 perfume compositions showing that deviations from a pairwise maximum-entropy model are organized around shared item pairs, and that adding three-body couplings for 50 triplets improves predictions across the remaining 19,550 triplets.
motivation: Pairwise maximum-entropy (Ising-like) models are widely used to describe co-occurrence data, but real datasets often contain genuine higher-order dependencies whose structure is poorly characterized; the authors ask whether such dependencies in perfume item combinations are organized rather than random.
method: The authors encode the 50 most frequently listed perfume items as binary variables, fit a pairwise maximum-entropy model, compare observed three-item marginals against synthetic refits, then introduce three-body couplings for 50 selected triplets and reoptimize all parameters, with a static linear-response calculation to explain parameter readjustment.
result: Strongly deviating triplets concentrate around shared item pairs, beyond what individual item frequencies explain; adding 50 three-body couplings reduces the sum of squared standardized residuals over the remaining 19,550 triplets by 5.44%, with larger reductions for triplets sharing an item pair, and linear response reproduces the co-occurrence changes with Pearson correlation 0.850.
conclusion: Higher-order statistical dependencies in compositional data are organized around shared lower-order structures, and a small number of three-body couplings can propagate systematically through the model; the framework is generic but is demonstrated only on classical consumer-composition data.

title: Fourier Crosstalk And Leakage Correction For Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
authors: Chongwu Shao, Yue Cao, Wei Zhang, Xiao-Peng Jin, Yinran Shen, Shijian Li, Xu-Ri Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital micromirror devices enable high-speed Fourier single-pixel imaging (Fourier-SPI), but their binary modulation introduces quantization errors that degrade the reconstructed image quality. In particular, each binarized Fourier probe contains non-target Fourier components, thereby distorting the corresponding Fourier-domain measurement. This Letter presents a Fourier domain correction framework that characterizes these errors using the Fourier-domain response matrix of the decoded binary Fourier patterns. Accordingly, a response-matrix-based Fourier-SPI measurement model is established by partitioning the matrix into components associated with the sampled and unsampled frequencies, thereby decomposing the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage. This model established a generalized correction framework, termed Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction (FCLC), alongside two simplified methods: Fourier Sampled-Frequency Crosstalk Correction (FSCC) and Fourier DC Crosstalk Correction (FDCC). FSCC is implemented via an inversion-free Richardson-type iteration, whereas FDCC admits a closed-form solution. Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies reveal that the proposed framework improves reconstruction fidelity without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.
tldr: A Fourier-domain correction framework is proposed to mitigate quantization errors in binary-encoded Fourier single-pixel imaging, improving reconstruction fidelity without altering the acquisition process.
motivation: Binary modulation by digital micromirror devices introduces crosstalk and leakage in Fourier single-pixel imaging, degrading image quality.
method: The authors characterize errors using a Fourier-domain response matrix and decompose the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage, leading to a generalized correction framework (FCLC) and two simplified methods (FSCC and FDCC).
result: Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies show improved reconstruction fidelity compared to uncorrected measurements.
conclusion: The proposed correction framework effectively reduces quantization artifacts in binary Fourier single-pixel imaging without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.

title: The Maximum Number Of Sets For 16 Cards Is 26
authors: Justin Stevens
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In SET, each card has four properties with three values each, and three cards form a when every property is all the same or all different. We prove that the maximum number of sets among [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] cards is [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], respectively. Viewing cards as points of [MATH] and sets as lines, we show that a configuration that leaves one of the [MATH] line directions of [MATH] unused projects into [MATH] without losing a set, which reduces the problem to three properties, where exhaustive search is feasible. We force an unused direction by counting repeated directions in the planes through a card on many sets, and treat configurations containing a magic square separately.
tldr: The paper determines the exact maximum number of SETs (lines) achievable by 16 cards in the four-property SET game, proving the answer is 26 via a reduction to three properties and exhaustive search.
motivation: The extremal combinatorics of the card game SET — i.e., how many collinear triples can a subset of F_3^4 contain — is a natural finite-geometry question whose exact small-case values were previously unknown.
method: Cards are identified with points of F_3^4 and sets with affine lines; the authors show that any configuration leaving one of the four line directions unused projects into F_3^3 without losing sets, and they force such an unused direction by counting repeated directions in planes through a card, treating magic-square configurations separately.
result: The maximum numbers of sets among 4, 8, 12, and 16 cards are proven to be exact values culminating in 26 for 16 cards, matching the reductions made feasible by exhaustive search in three dimensions.
conclusion: The work settles the extremal SET problem for small deck sizes and illustrates how geometric projection arguments can reduce combinatorial search to tractable size.

title: Support Recovery Of Diffusion Models Under The Manifold Hypothesis
authors: Ayya Alieva, Gautam Iyer, Alexei Novikov, Lenya Ryzhik
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis with possibly large score estimation and discretization errors, and show that while they may not exactly recover the data distribution, they will exactly recover the support (or data manifold). In continuous time, we use a Lyapunov function to show that even if the relative score estimation error is fixed (and not necessarily vanishing), then the rate at which the process approaches the support is [MATH] as [MATH], where [MATH] is the final time. In discrete time, we use geometric time steps with a fixed (non-vanishing) ratio and show that with a fixed (also not small) relative score estimation error, the process approaches the data manifold exponentially with the number of iterations. The proof relies on controlling a Gaussian measure of a neighborhood of the cut-locus of the data manifold, using a polynomial approximation argument combined with quantitative semi-algebraic estimates.
tldr: The paper proves that diffusion models trained under the manifold hypothesis recover the data manifold (support) exactly, even with fixed, non-vanishing score estimation and discretization errors.
motivation: Diffusion models are widely used generative models, yet it is unclear what they converge to when score estimation is imperfect; the authors ask whether the support of the distribution, rather than the distribution itself, can be reliably recovered.
method: They construct a Lyapunov function for the continuous-time reverse process and, for discrete time, use geometric time steps with a fixed ratio, controlling a Gaussian measure of a neighborhood of the cut-locus of the manifold via polynomial approximation and quantitative semi-algebraic estimates.
result: In continuous time the process approaches the support at a rate of order 1/T in the final time T with fixed relative score error, and in discrete time it approaches the manifold exponentially in the number of iterations despite non-small relative score error.
conclusion: Diffusion models are robust in the sense that their samples concentrate on the true data manifold even when the learned score is inaccurate, though exact recovery of the full data distribution is not guaranteed.

title: Two-Sided Projection-Based Model Reduction Of Parametric Generalized Algebraic Riccati Equations Via Grassmann-Manifold Optimization
authors: Xuelian Wen, Qiuqi Li, Juan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations arise in many-query problems in optimal control, state estimation, and filtering, where repeated full-order solutions may become computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this paper, within a projection-based model reduction framework, we propose a two-sided projection approach that constructs reduced bases by minimizing the aggregate relative two-sided projection error of Riccati solution snapshots. Under suitable dissipativity assumptions, the resulting Galerkin-projected PGARE admits a unique symmetric positive semidefinite stabilizing solution. For error assessment, we employ an existing residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the full-order Riccati residual. A projection-based error decomposition developed in this work provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed basis construction. To accommodate clustered solution manifolds, we extend the framework to localized model reduction by combining parameter-space proximity and solution-space correlation for clustering, with classifier-based online basis selection. Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed global and localized approaches in terms of approximation accuracy and computational efficiency.
tldr: The paper develops two-sided projection-based model reduction for parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations using Grassmann-manifold optimization and localized bases.
motivation: Repeated full-order solves of parametric Riccati equations are computationally prohibitive in many-query optimal control, estimation, and filtering applications.
method: Reduced bases are constructed by minimizing aggregate relative two-sided projection error over solution snapshots on a Grassmann manifold, with a localized clustering and classifier-based online basis selection extension.
result: Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems show improved approximation accuracy and computational efficiency for both global and localized approaches.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides an effective model-reduction strategy for parametric Riccati equations, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Field Algebras Associated With Non-symmetric Lattices
authors: Mohamed Wacyl Meddour
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice [MATH] equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra [MATH], generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.
tldr: The paper develops a structure theory of Bakalov–Kac field algebras, proving a reconstruction theorem and constructing canonical field algebras from finite-rank lattices with non-symmetric bilinear forms.
motivation: Field algebras generalize vertex algebras by weakening locality to an associativity-type axiom, and the author aims to handle geometric examples where the natural bilinear form is not symmetric, a case excluded by standard vertex algebra theory.
method: Abstract algebraic and representation-theoretic techniques are used: a reconstruction theorem builds a field algebra from a generating family of fields, and lattice-based constructions generalize Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras; commutants are analyzed as subfield algebras.
result: Every finite-rank lattice with an arbitrary bilinear form is shown to yield a canonical field algebra, and these constructions are realized geometrically via the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending work of Dominic Joyce.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational algebraic framework extending vertex algebra theory to non-symmetric settings with geometric applications, but remains purely within pure mathematics.

title: Self-adjoint Boundary Conditions For Equation-free Multiscale Modelling
authors: J. E. Bunder
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.
tldr: The paper develops equation-free multiscale modelling schemes that preserve self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models governed by compact self-adjoint operators on bounded domains.
motivation: Patch coupling conditions in equation-free modelling must preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation, otherwise macroscale simulations can violate conservation laws and produce unphysical results.
method: The authors design coupling conditions at patch boundaries that maintain self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by compact self-adjoint operators with fixed boundary conditions.
result: The new construction yields equation-free simulations that respect the symmetry and conservation properties of the underlying microscale problem, extending applicability to a broader class of systems.
conclusion: Self-adjoint-preserving patch coupling widens the range of systems amenable to equation-free multiscale modelling while ensuring physically consistent macroscale dynamics.

title: Quasi-product And Multiplicative Markov Measures Radon-Nikodym Problem, Random Walks: The Free Group Case
authors: Vadim A. Kaimanovich
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.
tldr: The paper clarifies the role of multiplicative Markov measures on topological Markov chains by linking them to the Radon-Nikodym problem for product cocycles and harmonic measures of nearest-neighbour random walks on free groups.
motivation: The work aims to conceptually unify special measures on topological Markov chains with random-walk harmonic measures via the Radon-Nikodym cocycle structure on the free group boundary.
method: It combines ergodic-theoretic and probabilistic arguments, interpreting multiplicative Markov measures as unique solutions to a Radon-Nikodym problem and showing that the harmonic measure cocycle for nearest-neighbour random walks is a product cocycle.
result: The main result establishes that multiplicative Markov measures on the free group boundary correspond to unique Radon-Nikodym solutions for product cocycles, yielding a structural link with harmonic measures of random walks.
conclusion: The paper provides a conceptual clarification of multiplicative Markov measures in random-walk settings, but it is a pure probability/ergodic-theory contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
authors: Leonard J. E. Pleschberger
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on [MATH] or unilaterally on [MATH], inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gau\ss ian constant [MATH] with the lemniscate constant [MATH] by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $[MATH][MATH][MATH]$ This machinery proves conjectures on lattice sums arising in electrostatics proposed by Vigren and Dieckmann (Symmetry, 2020).
tldr: The paper introduces three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions and computes normalization constants via elliptic integrals and lemniscate constants.
motivation: The work is inspired by Ramanujan's series evaluations and aims to resolve conjectures on lattice sums arising in electrostatics.
method: The authors define bilateral and unilateral discrete distributions, explicitly evaluate relevant series, and express normalization constants using singular values of complete elliptic integrals and Gauss's constant.
result: Exact normalization constants are obtained, and conjectures by Vigren and Dieckmann on lattice sums in electrostatics are proven.
conclusion: The paper provides new mathematical probability distributions and series identities, with applications to lattice sums, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dual-Mode Extremum Seeking For A Class Of Unknown Controlled Diffusions
authors: Martin Guay, Shimin Wang, Edward Z. Cao, Stefan Damjanovic
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A dual-mode extremum-seeking controller is developed for unknown nonlinear systems with affine control inputs driven by persistent Brownian process noise. The controller uses a single measured cost, without state estimation or differentiation of the measurement. Bounded cosine feedback generates, through Lie-bracket averaging, a proportional--integral (PI) action: the proportional action stabilizes a feasible minimum of the cost on the time scale of the plant, and the integral action adapts a bias toward the unknown input that regulates the plant at that minimum. The averaged closed loop is a PI-regulated diffusion that retains the process noise, and its stability condition does not require knowledge of the control direction. Under a regional Lyapunov condition on the averaged dynamics, an exact periodic response of the noise-free closed loop is constructed and serves as the center of a Lyapunov function with bounds uniform in the excitation frequency. Exit-probability estimates show that, for small noise and large excitation frequency, trajectories reach a prescribed neighborhood of the optimum and remain there for times exponential in the inverse noise variance, with exponentially small failure probability. Under an additional stochastic contraction condition, the closed loop is approximated uniformly in time, in mean square before common exit, by its averaged diffusion driven by the same Brownian motion, with an error that decreases with the excitation frequency. The regional regulation conditions are verified for a planar hydrodynamic trap with an unknown stagnation-point offset and actuator sign. Simulations illustrate intensity-only confinement of a Brownian particle, integral compensation of the holding input, and axial-strip exit statistics.
tldr: A dual-mode extremum-seeking controller is developed for unknown nonlinear stochastic systems with affine inputs driven by Brownian noise, using only a single noisy cost measurement.
motivation: Extremum seeking typically assumes deterministic plants or requires state estimation and differentiation of measurements; the authors aim to extend it to unknown controlled diffusions without knowledge of the control direction.
method: Bounded cosine dithering combined with Lie-bracket averaging yields a PI-regulated averaged diffusion; stability is analyzed via regional Lyapunov functions, exit-probability estimates, and a stochastic contraction condition for averaging error bounds.
result: For small noise and high excitation frequency, trajectories reach a neighborhood of the optimum and stay there for times exponential in inverse noise variance with exponentially small failure probability; simulations show intensity-only confinement of a Brownian particle in a hydrodynamic trap with unknown offset and actuator sign.
conclusion: The scheme provides rigorous stochastic stability and averaging guarantees for model-free optimization of diffusive plants, with demonstrated applicability to optical trapping control.

title: Pole Rigidity In Root-optimal Rational Approximation Of The Exponential On Infinite Sectors
authors: Tianqi Zhang Fei Xue
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than [MATH], the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many [MATH]-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.
tldr: The paper proves weak convergence of normalized pole-counting measures for root-optimal rational approximations of the exponential on infinite sectors.
motivation: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical, but the limiting distribution of poles for general sectors of positive opening was not established.
method: The authors analyze reduced root-optimal sequences, rule out boundary pole accumulation, and control an exponentially small Hermite residual using reflection and noncancellation techniques without assuming interpolation or orthogonality.
result: They show that scaled pole-counting measures converge weakly to a unique probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector, explicitly constructed via a Ferrers function zero and related to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation.
conclusion: The work extends pole-law results from the half-line to infinite sectors of positive opening and provides a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many functions with a common denominator.

title: Mean-field Token Steering
authors: Md Zulfiqur Haider, Asmaa Eldesoukey, Abhishek Halder, Yongxin Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schr\"odinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.
tldr: The paper formulates stochastic token steering through transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for interacting particles on the unit sphere, solved via a spherical mean-field Schrödinger bridge and a generalized dynamic Sinkhorn recursion.
motivation: Steering the population of token representations inside a deep transformer stack is treated as a control problem, aiming to guide tokens toward a desired aggregate configuration in representation space with minimal control effort.
method: The attention-induced interaction is captured in a mean-field limit as a controlled integro-PDE on the unit sphere; minimum-effort control over normalized layer depth is derived and identified with a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to sphere geometry, computed by a generalized dynamic Sinkhorn recursion.
result: Numerical experiments reportedly achieve exact steering of the token population under the proposed recursive scheme.
conclusion: Mean-field optimal control and Schrödinger-bridge methods provide a principled and computationally tractable framework for steering transformer token distributions, though the work lies outside quantum information science.

title: Learning The Average Dose-Response Function With A Right-Censored Treatment
authors: Yifan Cui Sihan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation.
