The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, applies area bounds to complementary unit-sided polygons, and excludes the remaining cases by exact angle certificates. The supplement contains 13,668 stored marked records, 233 exclusion certificates, a standard-library verifier, and independent checks of the complete enumeration.
tldr: The paper proves minimal triangle counts for strict unit-triangle configurations with one or two poles, including a sharp bound attained by the double kite.
motivation: The work concerns extremal questions about finite connected families of equilateral unit triangles and their contact graphs, a problem in discrete and combinatorial geometry.
method: The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, uses area bounds for complementary unit-sided polygons, and rules out remaining cases with exact angle certificates and computer-assisted verification.
result: Every strict configuration with one or two poles contains at least fourteen triangles, with the bound sharp for two poles via the double kite and reverse double kite; related bounds of twenty-eight and forty-two triangles are also established.
conclusion: The paper settles minimality questions for strict two-pole triangle configurations and provides enumerated records and certificates supporting the proof.

title: Optimal Capital Injections In A Microlending Group Under External Shocks
authors: H\'ector Jasso-Fuentes, Alejandra Quintos, Xinta Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.19028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by static models of group default in microlending, we study a dynamic problem in which the members of a lending group are exposed to external shocks, such as droughts or floods, and the manager of a common emergency fund decides at each shock how much capital to inject into the members who were hit. Shocks arrive at random times, the set of members that a shock hits may depend on which members the previous shock hit, and the losses may spill over to members who were not hit directly. Between shocks, the members' wealth follows a linear stochastic differential equation in which members support each other, and the fund grows with interest and member contributions up to a cap. The cost balances the members' shortfall below a poverty line, a welfare measure that contains a standard poverty measure as a special case, against the administrative cost of the injections and the benefit of keeping money in the fund. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process embedded at the shock times and prove that the embedded process is Markov with a weakly continuous transition kernel. When the discount rate exceeds a growth rate determined by the wealth dynamics, we show that the expected total cost is finite under every policy, that the finite-horizon optimal values converge to the infinite-horizon one at an explicit rate, and that there exists a stationary optimal injection policy, which can be chosen independent of calendar time.
tldr: The paper studies optimal capital injection policies for a common emergency fund in a microlending group facing random external shocks, formulated as a Markov decision process embedded at shock times.
motivation: Motivated by static models of group default in microlending, the authors aim to understand how a fund manager should dynamically allocate capital to members hit by shocks such as droughts or floods, while accounting for spillover losses and poverty-line shortfalls.
method: Members' wealth evolves via a coupled linear stochastic differential equation between shocks; shocks arrive at random times with state-dependent hit sets. The problem is cast as an MDP embedded at shock epochs, with the transition kernel shown to be weakly continuous.
result: Under a discount rate exceeding a growth rate set by the wealth dynamics, the expected total cost is finite for every policy, finite-horizon optimal values converge to the infinite-horizon value at an explicit rate, and a stationary, calendar-time-independent optimal injection policy exists.
conclusion: The framework provides provable existence and convergence guarantees for optimal dynamic capital injection in group microlending, offering a tractable stochastic-control foundation for emergency-fund management under correlated external shocks.
